title: Unsynchronized cross-thread 'player' publication: in-flight inlineStart can start an orphaned, never-released MediaPlayer after inlineStop/onCleared (contract items 1, 2, 7)
evidence: Line 49: 'private var player: MediaPlayer? = null' - plain var, no @Volatile/Mutex. inlineStart runs the whole create-assign-start sequence on an IO thread: line 144 'scope.launch(Dispatchers.IO) {', lines 160-181 'val newPlayer = MediaPlayer().apply { .. prepare() .. }' then 'player = newPlayer' (176) and 'newPlayer.start()' (181). There is no suspension point between the coroutine's last resume (for local files: none at all after launch; for SMB: return from downloadSmbAudioToCache) and start(), so cooperative cancellation of viewModelScope is never observed in that window. inlineStop (lines 86-94, 'player?.let { .. it.release() }; player = null') runs on the main thread (BrowseActivity.onStop:639 'viewModel.inlineStop()', BrowseViewModel.onCleared:668, back-nav BrowseActivity:403/418). Runtime path A (screen leave): tap an SMB audio file (multi-second download) -> press Back/Home before prepare completes -> onStop + onCleared call inlineStop() which sees player==null and releases nothing -> the IO coroutine, already past its last suspension point, executes 'player = newPlayer; newPlayer.start()' on the field of the dead ViewModel -> audio keeps playing with no remaining code path that can release it (saveResumeState/prefetch launches on the cancelled scope are no-ops). Runtime path B (rapid track switch): 'else -> { inlineStop(); inlineStart(file) }' (lines 78-81) - tapping track B while track A's IO coroutine is between resolveLocalPath and line 176 produces two live MediaPlayers; both assign 'player' last-writer-wins and both call start() -> the losing instance is never released and two audio streams overlap. Not P0 only because the manager holds @ApplicationContext (BrowseViewModel.kt:60), so no Activity/View is retained.
fix_hint: Confine player mutation to one thread or guard with a generation token: capture an epoch/stop counter before launching inlineStart, and before 'player = newPlayer; start()' re-check it (under a Mutex or on Dispatchers.Main); if superseded or scope-inactive, release newPlayer immediately instead of assigning; also check 'isActive' after the blocking prepare().

title: Error path leaks the freshly created MediaPlayer: prepare()/setDataSource failure reaches catch that resets state but never calls release() (contract item 7)
evidence: Lines 160-175: 'val newPlayer = MediaPlayer().apply { try { setDataSource(localPath) } catch (e: java.io.IOException) { .. reset(); setDataSource(context, ..) .. else { throw e } } prepare(); setOnCompletionListener { inlinePlayNext() } }'. The inner try covers only the first setDataSource; 'prepare()' (line 173), the content-URI fallback 'setDataSource(context, ..)' (line 168), and the rethrow at line 170 all propagate to the outer handler, lines 185-188: 'catch (e: Exception) { Timber.e(e, "InlinePlayer: failed to start .."); _inlinePlayerState.value = InlinePlayerState() }' - no release() of the already-constructed native MediaPlayer, and 'player' was never assigned so inlineStop() can never reach it. Concrete trigger: a truncated/corrupt inline_audio cache file (e.g. produced by an interrupted earlier download) or an unsupported codec makes prepare() throw IOException -> one native MediaPlayer (codec/AudioTrack handles) is orphaned per failed tap, held until non-deterministic finalization; repeated retries on the same broken file accumulate unreleased players. Same catch also swallows CancellationException from the download suspension (broad 'catch (e: Exception)').
fix_hint: Wrap creation in try/catch that calls newPlayer.release() on any failure before rethrowing/logging (or use runCatching { .. }.onFailure { newPlayer.release() }); rethrow CancellationException separately.

title: Inline audio plays without ever requesting audio focus, so release has nothing to abandon and playback ignores focus loss (contract item 5)
evidence: Playback starts at line 181 'newPlayer.start()' and stops at lines 86-94 ('fun inlineStop() { player?.let { try { it.stop() } .. it.release() } .. }') with zero AudioManager/AudioFocusRequest usage anywhere in the class; grep over ui/browse shows audio-focus handling exists only in BrowseMicRecordingManager.kt (requestAudioFocus line 74/83, abandonAudioFocus lines 232-244) - nothing acquires focus on behalf of inline playback. Runtime path: user starts inline audio while another app plays music -> both streams mix (no AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN request), and when another app later takes focus (navigation prompt, incoming media app) inline audio keeps playing because no OnAudioFocusChangeListener exists. The release-side of item 5 is vacuous only because acquisition is missing entirely.
fix_hint: Request AudioFocusRequest(AUDIOFOCUS_GAIN) with an OnAudioFocusChangeListener (pause on transient loss, stop on loss) before start(), and abandonAudioFocusRequest in inlineStop(); mirror the existing BrowseMicRecordingManager pattern.

title: playerWarmupJob / audioMetadataEnrichmentJob / lastWarmupSignature written on IO dispatcher but cancelled/read from main thread without synchronization - cancel edge can miss the live job
evidence: Lines 60-62: 'private var playerWarmupJob: Job? = null .. private var audioMetadataEnrichmentJob: Job? = null' - plain vars. Writers run on the IO dispatcher: schedulePlayerWarmupIfEligible (lines 288-292: 'lastWarmupSignature = sig; playerWarmupJob?.cancel(); playerWarmupJob = scope.launch {..}') is invoked from coroutines launched with 'scope.launch(ioDispatcher + exceptionHandler)' in BrowseResourceLoadManager (launch sites lines 105 and 312; call sites lines 216, 265, 467), and enrichAudioMetadataInBackground (lines 210-211: 'audioMetadataEnrichmentJob?.cancel(); audioMetadataEnrichmentJob = scope.launch(ioDispatcher + exceptionHandler)') is called from the same IO coroutine via onFilesLoadedSaveAndEnrich (BrowseViewModel.kt:471). Readers run on main: cancelPlayerWarmup() (lines 309-311) <- BrowseViewModel.cancelScan:736 <- BrowseActivity.onStop:642, and cancelAll() (lines 314-317) <- BrowseViewModel.onCleared:663. With no @Volatile/Mutex the main thread can read a stale null/old Job and skip cancelling the just-assigned one (e.g. onStop's 'cancelScan(forceCancel = true)' misses a warmup scheduled concurrently by the finishing load). P2 not P1 because impact is bounded: all jobs are viewModelScope children (killed at clear anyway) and the warmup player self-releases in the same statement (line 296 'ExoPlayer.Builder(context).build().release()') - no resource can remain held.
fix_hint: Confine job-field mutation to the main dispatcher (make schedulePlayerWarmupIfEligible hop via withContext(Dispatchers.Main) for the assignment) or mark the fields @Volatile and do cancel-and-assign under a small Mutex.

title: inline_audio disk cache has no size bound or eviction: every played/prefetched SMB track is stored in full, forever, until a manual whole-cache wipe or OS storage pressure
evidence: Lines 241-245: 'val cacheDir = java.io.File(context.cacheDir, "inline_audio"); cacheDir.mkdirs(); return java.io.File(cacheDir, "${file.path.hashCode()}_${file.name}")' - and downloadSmbAudioToCache writes the entire remote file (line 292 'java.io.FileOutputStream(cacheFile).use { output -> smbClient.get().downloadFile(..) }'); prefetchNextInlineAudio (lines 202-221) additionally downloads the next track automatically after every start. Grep for 'inline_audio' across app_v2/src/main finds only this method - no size check, LRU trim, or age-based cleanup exists on the write path or anywhere else; the only deletions are the per-file failure cleanup (line 309 'cacheFile.delete()') and the user-triggered Settings 'Clear cache' which wipes the whole cacheDir (GeneralSettingsCacheHelper.kt:127-128 'val cacheDir = fragment.requireContext().cacheDir; deleteRecursive(cacheDir)'). Runtime path: listening through a large SMB music share caches every track at full size (play + prefetch), consuming storage equal to the share's audio volume until the user manually clears cache or the OS trims app cache under low-storage pressure. P2 rather than P1 because cacheDir is OS-evictable and a manual wipe exists, so growth is not strictly unbounded on-device.
fix_hint: Add a bound on the write path: after a successful download, trim inline_audio to a max size (e.g. delete oldest-mtime files beyond N MB), or reuse UnifiedFileCache which already has stats/clearAll infrastructure.

title: Pending MediaController future overwritten without release - orphaned bound controller pins AudioPlaybackService (and its ExoPlayer) past stopSelf, so onDestroy/release can never run
evidence: connect() guards only on completed connections: `if (isConnected)` (line 51) where `val isConnected: Boolean get() = mediaController?.isConnected == true` (lines 39-40) is false for the whole async connect window. It then unconditionally overwrites the stored future: `val future = MediaController.Builder(context, sessionToken).buildAsync(); controllerFuture = future` (lines 63-64); connectForStatus() does the same at lines 257-258. release() releases only the LAST stored future: `controllerFuture?.let { MediaController.releaseFuture(it) }` (line 311). Concrete path: PlayerActivity resumes on a photo while background audio runs -> NowPlayingManager.updateBarVisibility calls `audioServiceController.connectForStatus { .. }` (NowPlayingManager.kt:155) -> future F1 pending; user navigates to an audio file within the connect window (on cold service start the window spans service onCreate incl. ExoPlayer build) -> PlayerMediaLoaderManager -> `audioServiceController.playAudioPlaylistWithMetadata(items, startIndex, onPlayerReady)` (NowPlayingManager.kt:98) -> connect() sees isConnected==false -> builds F2, `controllerFuture = F2`, F1 is orphaned. F1 completes and its MediaController stays bound to AudioPlaybackService for the process lifetime (never passed to MediaController.releaseFuture; PlayerLifecycleManager.kt:190 `activity.audioServiceController?.release()` releases only F2). Android does not destroy a service with bound clients: after playback ends, AudioPlaybackService.autoStopRunnable `stopSelf()` (AudioPlaybackService.kt:87) and MainActivity `stopService(serviceIntent)` (MainActivity.kt:1423-1428) never reach onDestroy, so `mediaSession?.run { player.release(); release() }` (AudioPlaybackService.kt:417-420) never executes - the ExoPlayer and MediaSession stay alive unreleased and `isRunning` remains true (misdrives MainActivity restore-player at MainActivity.kt:335-349 and exit logic). Violates contract items 2/7 (player instance survives its teardown edge unreleased) and the unit-note 'binder clients not retaining the service'.
fix_hint: In connect()/connectForStatus(), when a previous connect is in flight, attach the callback to the existing pending future instead of building a new one; if replacement is intended, call MediaController.releaseFuture(previousFuture) before overwriting controllerFuture.

title: onDestroy final-position save is cancelled by serviceScope.cancel() on the next statement - the destroy-edge save is dead in practice
evidence: AudioPlaybackService.onDestroy lines 405-414: `if (path != null && finalDur > 0 && finalPos >= 0) { serviceScope.launch(Dispatchers.IO) { try { playbackPositionRepository.savePosition(path, finalPos, finalDur) } catch (e: Exception) { Timber.e(e, "AudioPlaybackService: onDestroy save position failed") } } }` followed immediately by `serviceScope.cancel()` (line 414). The launched coroutine is a child of serviceScope (`CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob() + Dispatchers.Main)`, line 91); cancel() on the very next statement cancels it before the IO dispatcher runs it, or at its first suspension point - savePosition is suspend end-to-end (PlaybackPositionRepository.kt:14 `suspend fun savePosition(..)` -> Room suspend DAO PlaybackPositionDao.kt:15 `suspend fun savePosition(position: PlaybackPositionEntity)`), so the Room write aborts. The `catch (e: Exception)` at line 409 additionally swallows the CancellationException and logs it as a save failure. Runtime path: network-audio (currentOriginalPath non-empty) playing -> user stops the service mid-track (auto-stop, fatal error stopSelf, MainActivity exit stopService, task-removed stop) -> onDestroy runs -> the code that comments 'Capture position before player is released' (lines 399-403) computes finalPos/finalDur but the persistence coroutine is cancelled -> resume position falls back to the last periodic tick, up to POSITION_SAVE_INTERVAL_MS = 15_000L (line 117) stale. Cleanup-path work defeated by its own teardown ordering (protocol: 'failure paths clean up resources too'); bounded position loss -> P2.
fix_hint: Launch the final save with NonCancellable (`serviceScope.launch(Dispatchers.IO + NonCancellable) { .. }`) or into an injected application-scoped CoroutineScope, and only then cancel serviceScope; rethrow CancellationException in the catch.

title: Swap-to-next-file never releases the previous ExoPlayer: every paged/renamed video orphans a live player (and its AudioFocusManager) that survives host teardown
evidence: playVideo() unconditionally builds a new player and overwrites the owner field without releasing the previous instance: lines 380-381 'val player = ExoPlayer.Builder(activity).build(); exoPlayer = player', and lines 385-388 overwrite 'audioFocusManager = AudioFocusManager(activity) {...}; audioFocusManager?.requestFocus()' without calling releaseFocus() on the old one. show() (lines 259-277) and hidePhotoAndPlayerViews() (lines 686-690, visibility toggles only) never stop/release the player when the next file is IMAGE/GIF, and the old player still has playWhenReady=true from line 392, so paging video->image leaves the previous video's audio playing behind the photo. release() (lines 317-323) tears down only the CURRENT 'exoPlayer' - all previously orphaned instances are unreachable to it and are never released (an unreleased ExoPlayer keeps its internal playback HandlerThread alive; release() is the only call that quits it). Reachable from the unit host on every file swap: PhotoVideoStandaloneActivity.observeData() lines 814-818 'if (file.path != lastShownPath) { ... viewManager.show(file, type, onVideoReady); lastShownPath = file.path }', driven by pageNext/pagePrevious/pageRandom/slideshow (StandalonePlayerViewModel.publishCurrentFile swaps state.mediaFile; VIDEO is host-supported via setHostSupportedTypes(IMAGE,GIF,VIDEO), activity line 789) and by rename (onRenameComplete rewrites mediaFile.path -> re-show of the same video with a new URI while the old player keeps playing). Each orphaned player also permanently retains activity-referencing listeners that are never removed (contract item 4): the error listener added at line 384 'player.addListener(createPlayerErrorListener())' (anonymous inner of the manager, which holds 'activity'), plus the anonymous tracks listener added per video in PhotoVideoStandaloneActivity.setupVideoControls() lines 970-977 'viewManager.getExoPlayer()?.addListener(object : Player.Listener {...})' with no removeListener anywhere. Violates contract items 1 (duplicate/orphan creation path), 7 (swap-to-next-file path does not release) and 4 (listeners on orphaned instances never removed). The unified host is immune only because it shows content once ('if (!contentLoaded)', StandalonePlayerActivity line 942) - this per-type host added paging on top of show-once glue, the exact family divergence the unit note warns about. Escalates toward P0 retained-Activity (orphaned player -> live playback thread -> listeners -> activity) pending LeakCanary confirmation per the evidence ladder.
fix_hint: Extract a releaseCurrentVideoPlayer() that mirrors the release() block (setVideoEffects(emptyList()), clearVideoSurface(), stop(), release(), audioFocusManager?.releaseFocus()) and call it at the top of playVideo() and in show() before the IMAGE/GIF/other branches; also stop position auto-save for the old file there.

title: Glide loads bind the app-lifetime RequestManager to the activity's photoView and are never cleared, so the tracked target (and its activity context) outlives host destroy
evidence: All three image paths load via the application-context RequestManager into the host activity's ImageView: showImage() lines 343-345 'Glide.with(activity.applicationContext).load(mediaFile.path.toUri()).into(safeViews.photoView)', reloadImage() lines 355-360 and showGif() lines 366-369 (same pattern). Grep over the unit confirms no Glide.clear()/RequestManager.clear() exists anywhere: neither release() (lines 293-334) nor PhotoVideoStandaloneActivity.onDestroy() (lines 1013-1024) clears the target. An application-context RequestManager is bound to ApplicationLifecycle, so its requests are not cancelled and its TargetTracker entries are not released when the activity is destroyed - the last ViewTarget for photoView stays tracked for the process lifetime, strongly holding the destroyed activity's ImageView (and through View.mContext the activity), and an in-flight full-size decode continues after back-press. Violates contract item 9 (Glide targets in the unit cleared on detach) and the protocol Layer 3 Glide rule ('clear(target) on detach; do not bind Glide.with(activity) to a long-lived target' - here inverted: a long-lived manager bound to an activity view, the documented leak pattern). Concrete path: open any image/gif standalone -> press back -> activity destroyed while the app-scoped RequestManager still tracks its photoView; repeated opens accumulate one retained view hierarchy each. Matches the P0 retained-View pattern; kept at P1 because retention proof requires the LeakCanary rung, which a read-only audit cannot run.
fix_hint: Use Glide.with(activity) (lifecycle-aware, auto-clears on destroy) for photoView loads, or add Glide.with(activity.applicationContext).clear(safeViews.photoView) to StandaloneViewManager.release().

title: Player released on onDestroy instead of the API24+ onStop edge, with no documenting comment for the deviation - codecs held while the host sits stopped in background
evidence: Teardown edges: onPause() lines 1006-1011 only sets playWhenReady=false via viewManager.onPause() ('val isInPip = ...; if (!isInPip) viewManager.onPause()'), and the player is released only in onDestroy() lines 1013-1024 ('viewManager.release()' line 1022). There is no onStop/onStart pair, so on API 24+ (minSdk 26) a HOME-press or multi-window focus loss leaves the prepared ExoPlayer with its codec resources held for the entire stopped-in-background lifetime until the framework finally destroys the activity. Contract item 2 requires release in onStop / re-create in onStart 'or a deliberate documented alternative': the only nearby comment (line 1007, 'S0393 U1: keep playback running when the activity pauses to enter PiP') documents the PiP pause exception, not the choice of the onDestroy release edge. Mirrors the unified host exactly (StandalonePlayerActivity.onPause lines 437-443 / onDestroy line 455 'viewManager.release()'), so this is family-consistent rather than divergence, and the player IS released on real teardown - hence P2 (missing lifecycle-awareness without a proven leak), not P1.
fix_hint: Either release in onStop and rebuild/restore position in onStart (guard with isInPictureInPictureMode, since onStop does not fire while pipped), or add an explicit comment at onDestroy documenting the deliberate alternative (PiP keep-alive + configChanges no-recreate rationale).

title: Service-mode play() callback has no staleness guard: playback starts after stop(), leaving an orphaned playing service player with all inline-UI state cleared
evidence: play() service branch: `audioController.playAudioWithMetadata(Uri.parse(source.url), source.title) { startedPlayer -> player = startedPlayer; startedPlayer.addListener(playerListener) }` (lines 126-129). The controller connect is asynchronous (`MediaController.Builder(context, sessionToken).buildAsync()` + `future.addListener(...)`, AudioServiceController.kt:63-77) and the connect callback unconditionally starts playback: `player.setMediaItem(mediaItem) ... player.prepare(); player.play(); onPlayerReady(player)` (AudioServiceController.kt:148-152). Neither stop() nor a new play() cancels the pending connect, and the onPlayerReady lambda never checks that its source is still current. Concrete path (double-tap toggle, service cold): tap an AUDIO row -> play(bg=true) sets currentSource/playingId synchronously and starts the async connect; tap the same row again inside the connect window -> StreamsActivity.onPlay sees `inlineAudio.playingId == source.id` and calls stop() -> stopPlaybackKeepingController() runs with `player == null` so `player?.stop()` is a no-op (lines 174-190), state cleared (`currentSource = null`, `usingService = false`), mini-control hidden. The connect then completes -> the foreground service starts audible playback AFTER the user stopped it, and the manager re-enters `player = startedPlayer; startedPlayer.addListener(playerListener)` with `playingId == null`, `isServiceAudioActive == false`, `miniControl.isVisible == false`: an actively-streaming player with no visible stop control and no state flag claiming ownership (isLocalPlaybackActive and isServiceAudioActive are both false, so host onStop does nothing). It keeps playing until the user starts another stream or the Activity is destroyed (release() -> player?.stop()). Violates contract items 1 (orphan creation path) and 7 (stop/early-exit path does not cover the pending async start). Unowned actively-playing heavy resource = P1.
fix_hint: Guard the callback with a generation/source token: capture `source` (or a monotonically increasing request id) at play() and inside onPlayerReady bail out - `if (currentSource?.id != source.id) { startedPlayer.stop(); return }` - and/or add an AudioServiceController.cancelPendingConnect() invoked from stopPlaybackKeepingController().

title: connect() overwrites an in-flight controllerFuture: rapid second play() creates a duplicate MediaController that is never released and keeps playerListener attached forever
evidence: connect(): `if (isConnected) { ... return }` where `isConnected` is `mediaController?.isConnected == true` (lines 39-40, 51) - false while the FIRST connect is still pending because `mediaController` is only assigned inside the future listener (line 69). Then `val future = MediaController.Builder(context, sessionToken).buildAsync(); controllerFuture = future` (lines 63-64) unconditionally replaces the single-slot field without releasing/cancelling the previous pending future. release() disposes only the last slot: `controllerFuture?.let { MediaController.releaseFuture(it) }; controllerFuture = null; mediaController = null` (lines 311-313). Concrete path: on the streams screen with the service not yet connected, tap station A then station B before A's connect completes (StreamInlineAudioManager.play -> playAudioWithMetadata -> connect creates F2 while F1 is pending). Both futures complete: each callback assigns `mediaController = controller` and calls onConnected, so the manager runs `player = startedPlayer; startedPlayer.addListener(playerListener)` for BOTH controllers (StreamInlineAudioManager.kt:126-129), while stopPlaybackKeepingController()/release() remove the listener only from the current `player` reference (`player?.removeListener(playerListener)`, StreamInlineAudioManager.kt:174). Result: one connected MediaController to the foreground service session is never passed to MediaController.releaseFuture and never release()d, with a Player.Listener (referencing the manager and its host Views) permanently attached to it. Violates contract items 1 (duplicate creation path) and 4 (added listener with no removal path). Unreleased player-interface resource = P1.
fix_hint: Before creating a new future, dispose the in-flight one (`controllerFuture?.let(MediaController::releaseFuture)`), or track a pending flag and queue onConnected callbacks onto the single in-flight future instead of building a second controller. Apply the same to connectForStatus().

title: OFF-mode local ExoPlayer requests no audio focus and no becoming-noisy handling, unlike its service-mode twin
evidence: Local branch of play(): `val local = ExoPlayer.Builder(miniControl.context).setMediaSourceFactory(DefaultMediaSourceFactory(httpFactory)).build()` (lines 136-138) - no `setAudioAttributes(attrs, /* handleAudioFocus = */ true)` and no `setHandleAudioBecomingNoisy(true)`; ExoPlayer's defaults do not request audio focus and do not pause on ACTION_AUDIO_BECOMING_NOISY. The mirrored ON-mode player explicitly sets both: `.setAudioAttributes(audioAttributes, true).setHandleAudioBecomingNoisy(true)` (AudioPlaybackService.kt:197-198), proving the project contract for this audio family. Runtime path: with 'Background playback' OFF, every inline radio play() overlays any other app's audio (music app keeps playing simultaneously - no focus request means it is never paused/ducked, and the radio does not pause for calls/navigation prompts), and unplugging headphones keeps the stream blasting on the loudspeaker. Violates contract item 5 (audio-focus discipline) on the local branch; no leak, so P2.
fix_hint: Mirror the service builder: `.setAudioAttributes(AudioAttributes.Builder().setContentType(C.AUDIO_CONTENT_TYPE_MUSIC).setUsage(C.USAGE_MEDIA).build(), true).setHandleAudioBecomingNoisy(true)` on the local ExoPlayer.Builder chain.

title: stop() leaves playWhenReady=true and the playlist loaded on the service player, defeating AudioPlaybackService.onTaskRemoved's no-active-playback stopSelf heuristic
evidence: Service branch of stopPlaybackKeepingController(): `player?.stop()` (line 183) - Media3 Player.stop() transitions to STATE_IDLE but does not reset playWhenReady and does not clear media items. AudioPlaybackService.onTaskRemoved (AudioPlaybackService.kt:381-391) decides whether to stop: `if (currentPlayer == null || !currentPlayer.playWhenReady || currentPlayer.mediaItemCount == 0 || currentPlayer.playbackState == Player.STATE_ENDED) { ... stopSelf() } // If still playing, let the service continue`. After the user stops an inline ON-mode stream, the service player is IDLE with playWhenReady still true and mediaItemCount 1, so every disjunct is false and onTaskRemoved skips stopSelf for a service that is NOT playing anything. The service's own auto-stop timer is armed only on STATE_ENDED (AudioPlaybackService.kt:206-219); the STATE_IDLE branch (lines 235-238) only stops position saving. Concrete path: play inline radio with background playback ON -> tap the mini-control stop -> swipe the app away from recents -> the idle service (with its ExoPlayer and MediaSession) is deliberately left running by the misfired heuristic instead of stopping. Violates contract item 5 ('playWhenReady reset') and weakens item 7 (onTaskRemoved early-exit path); lifetime is ultimately bounded by OS background-service limits, hence P2 not P1.
fix_hint: In the service branch of stopPlaybackKeepingController(), also reset the flag before/after stop: `player?.playWhenReady = false` (or `player?.clearMediaItems()`), so onTaskRemoved and any 'is playback active' heuristics see a truly inactive player; alternatively arm the service auto-stop on STATE_IDLE too.

title: playAudio() creates a new AudioServiceController per track and orphans the previous one - connected MediaController (bound ServiceConnection to AudioPlaybackService) is never released on swap-to-next-file
evidence: StandaloneViewManager.playAudio() (lines 439-456): `val controller = AudioServiceController(activity)` / `audioServiceController = controller` - the field is overwritten unconditionally; the previous controller's `release()` is never called. AudioServiceController.release() (AudioServiceController.kt lines 307-314) is the ONLY place `MediaController.releaseFuture(it)` runs, and viewManager.release() (lines 325-327) releases only the CURRENT `audioServiceController`. Each controller is a live connection: `MediaController.Builder(context, sessionToken).buildAsync()` (AudioServiceController.kt line 63) binds to AudioPlaybackService using the Activity context (`AudioServiceController(activity)`) and stays registered with the service's MediaSession until released. Concrete runtime path in this unit: AudioStandaloneActivity.observeData() lines 519-522 `if (file.path != lastShownPath) { viewManager.show(file, MediaType.AUDIO) ... }`; every pageNext/pagePrevious/pageRandom and every slideshow auto-advance tick (StandalonePlayerViewModel.applyPaging -> publishCurrentFile -> updateState{copy(mediaFile=file)}, lines 247-261) re-enters show() -> playAudio() -> one more never-released connected MediaController. A slideshow over an audio folder (supportsSlideshow tracks folderPagingEnabled, AudioStandaloneActivity line 564) leaks one bound ServiceConnection + session-side controller registration per track, unbounded, for the whole activity lifetime; at finish() only the last controller is released and the framework force-unbinds the rest with 'ServiceConnection leaked' errors. Violates contract items 1 (single owner, no orphan creation path) and 7 (swap-to-next-file must release) and the Media3 requirement that every buildAsync() controller be released.
fix_hint: Create the AudioServiceController once per host and reuse it for subsequent tracks (its connect() is already idempotent: `if (isConnected) { onConnected; return }`), or call `audioServiceController?.release()` before assigning the new controller in playAudio().

title: SAF rename restarts audio playback from position 0 (and leaks the just-swapped controller): path change from onRenameComplete re-triggers viewManager.show() because lastShownPath is not updated on rename
evidence: Rename flow (StandaloneFileOperationsHandler.kt lines 520-527) calls `onRenameComplete(newUri, newName)` then `updateAudioMediaItem(newUri)`. The VM (StandalonePlayerViewModel.onRenameComplete, lines 312-320) does `state.copy(mediaFile = state.mediaFile?.copy(name=newName, path=newUri.toString(), contentUri=newUri.toString()))` - state.mediaFile.path changes. updateAudioMediaItem performs the intended seamless swap (`player.replaceMediaItem(0, ...)`; `player.seekTo(currentPosition)`, StandaloneViewManager.kt lines 517-523, with the activity comment line 183 'A SAF rename must keep the background-service playback uninterrupted'). But the state collector then resumes on main with the new path and hits lines 519-522: `if (file.path != lastShownPath) { viewManager.show(file, MediaType.AUDIO); lastShownPath = file.path ... }` - lastShownPath still holds the pre-rename path, so show() -> playAudio() runs: a NEW AudioServiceController is created (orphaning the one that just did the seamless replaceMediaItem) and its onConnected does `player.setMediaItem(mediaItem); player.prepare(); player.play()` (AudioServiceController.kt lines 148-152), resetting the service player to position 0. Concrete trigger: rename the currently playing audio file via btnRenameCmd when SAF returns a new URI (`if (newUri != uri)`) - playback audibly restarts from the beginning, defeating the documented uninterrupted-rename contract.
fix_hint: Update lastShownPath inside the onRenameComplete wiring (it already knows newUri), or compare a rename-stable identity instead of raw path in the collector.

title: onResume() force-sets playWhenReady=true, overriding a user's manual pause across background/foreground
evidence: StandaloneViewManager.onResume() lines 281-284: `exoPlayer?.playWhenReady = true; audioServiceController?.player?.playWhenReady = true` - unconditional. Runtime path from this unit: user taps pause on the PlayerView controller, presses Home (onPause line 288 sets playWhenReady=false - by design, 'standalone must never continue audio in background'), returns to the activity -> AudioStandaloneActivity.onResumeWithViews() line 546 `viewManager.onResume()` -> playback resumes even though the user had explicitly paused. The paused/playing state prior to onPause is not captured, so user intent is lost on every foreground return. Behavioral defect only; no resource impact.
fix_hint: Capture `wasPlayingBeforePause` in onPause() and restore playWhenReady=true in onResume() only when it was true.

title: onDestroy calls viewManager.release() on uninitialized lateinit - deterministic crash on the probe early-exit path (contract item 7)
evidence: setupViews() returns BEFORE viewManager is assigned when a default-player probe URI arrives: lines 259-263 `if (isDefaultPlayerProbe) { Timber.d("StandalonePlayer: short-circuiting default-player probe before standalone init"); finish(); return }` precede line 266 `viewManager = StandaloneViewManager(...)`. onDestroy() (lines 445-457) guards the neighbours - line 446 `if (::lifecycleManager.isInitialized) lifecycleManager.onDestroy()`, line 447 `pipManager?.release()` - but line 455 is unguarded: `viewManager.release()` on `private lateinit var viewManager` (line 185). finish() from setupViews still runs the full teardown, so onDestroy throws UninitializedPropertyAccessException. title: Glide targets never cleared on teardown and loads bound to applicationContext - in-flight request retains ImageView/Activity past onDestroy (contract item 9)
evidence: All three image paths load via the application-scoped RequestManager: showImage lines 343-345 `Glide.with(activity.applicationContext).load(mediaFile.path.toUri()).into(safeViews.photoView)`, showGif lines 366-369 (`.asGif()` same pattern), reloadImage lines 355-360. An application-scoped RequestManager is not paused or cleared when the host Activity is destroyed, so an in-flight decode keeps its ViewTarget -> photoView -> Activity context reachable until the load completes, and the completed drawable is set on a dead view. release() (lines 293-334, the manager's teardown edge called from StandalonePlayerActivity.onDestroy) clears players, viewers, and focus but contains no `Glide.with(...).clear(safeViews.photoView)` - confirmed by reading the whole file: no clear() call exists anywhere in the class. title: Video ExoPlayer released only in onDestroy - prepared player and codecs held for unbounded time while the activity is stopped in background (contract item 2)
evidence: The only release edge is onDestroy() line 445-457 (`viewManager.release()` line 455). title: Save-position-on-release coroutine launched into lifecycleScope from onDestroy - dead code on API 29+ (scope already cancelled), and lastSavedPosition is marked before the write commits
evidence: release() lines 300-309: `if (pathToSave != null && pos > 0L ...) { lifecycleScope.launch(Dispatchers.IO) { playbackPositionRepository.savePosition(pathToSave, pos, dur) ... } }`. release() is invoked from StandalonePlayerActivity.onDestroy() (line 455). On API 29+ androidx lifecycle dispatches ON_DESTROY via Application.ActivityLifecycleCallbacks.onActivityPreDestroyed, which the framework fires in Activity.performDestroy() BEFORE the onDestroy() body runs - so lifecycleScope is already cancelled and this launch never executes; the comment above it ('a coroutine launched after release() would arrive too late') documents the intent of a safety-net save that in fact never runs on API 29+. Impact is bounded because onPause saves (line 289) and the 5s auto-save loop (lines 757-765, POSITION_SAVE_INTERVAL_MS = 5_000L) cover normal exits, but the net is dead exactly on the paths that skip onPause saving (PiP teardown, cancelled onPause write). Secondary defect in the same flow: saveCurrentPosition lines 777-781 sets `lastSavedPosition = position` BEFORE `withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { ...savePosition... }` - if the scope is cancelled mid-write the position is falsely marked saved and the release-time re-check `pos != lastSavedPosition` (line 300) then skips it too.

title: Full Room DB open + entire migration ladder executes synchronously on the main thread at first injection
evidence: provideAppDatabase() force-opens the DB inside the Hilt @Provides: `val db = buildDatabase(context); // Force-open to trigger migrations now (catch failures early); db.openHelper.writableDatabase` and on failure runs `context.deleteDatabase(DB_NAME)` plus DatabaseResetNotice.recordReset on the same thread. AppDatabase is resolved non-lazily on the main thread on every cold start: MainActivity.observeData() line 1088 `collectOnLifecycle(viewModel.state)` dereferences the `by viewModels()` delegate during Activity onCreate -> Hilt constructs MainViewModel whose constructor takes `resourceRepository: ResourceRepository` (MainViewModel.kt:121, non-Lazy) -> ResourceRepositoryImpl injects ResourceDao -> provideResourceDao(database: AppDatabase) -> provideAppDatabase runs writableDatabase on the main thread. FastMediaSorterApp/AppStartupInitializer keep all DB deps in dagger.Lazy and only touch them in Dispatchers.IO coroutines gated on firstFrameSignal (which fires AFTER onCreate), so nothing warms the DB off-main first. writableDatabase performs SQLite open + the full 1..38 migration chain; on upgrade, migrateSchemaToV18/recreateResourcesTableWithNonNullShowSubfolders and MIGRATION_21_22 recreate whole tables and copy every row (AppDatabase.kt:421-488, 215-275) - main-thread disk I/O on the cold-start critical path, ANR-grade on a populated DB. title: Widget onUpdate runs runBlocking Room read + GZIP BLOB decompress + Gson parse of the full cached file list on the main thread

title: M3U playlist import writes N rows as N separate transactions (no withTransaction), unlike the sibling mergeCatalog
evidence: `suspend fun addAllIgnoringDuplicates(sources: List<StreamSourceEntity>): Int { var inserted = 0; for (source in sources) { if (dao.insertIgnore(source) != -1L) inserted++ }; return inserted }` - called from ImportStreamPlaylistUseCase.kt:52 with every entry of a user-supplied M3U playlist (IPTV lists run to thousands of rows; the same file's S0821 comment documents catalogs exceeding the 999 bind-variable limit). Each insertIgnore is its own implicit transaction (per-row fsync) and each invalidates stream_sources, so active collectors of observeAll/observePinned re-query and re-emit once per inserted row during the import; a process kill mid-loop leaves a partial import with no all-or-nothing boundary. The same class of defect was already fixed for mergeCatalog in this file: lines 74-77 'S0732: N update/insertIgnore writes plus the final catalog prune were not atomic... One transaction makes the catalog sync all-or-nothing (single observe* emission)' - addAllIgnoringDuplicates was left out. Violates Layer 4 'multi-step writes that must be atomic are wrapped in @Transaction'.
fix_hint: Wrap the loop in db.withTransaction { } (the AppDatabase handle is already injected), matching mergeCatalog.

title: insertAllAsOverrides is non-transactional and its hasOverrides() guard makes a partial apply permanent
evidence: `suspend fun insertAllAsOverrides(bindings: List<InputBinding>) { bindings.forEach { ... dao.upsert(InputBindingEntity(...)) } }` - a per-row upsert loop with no transaction. Sole caller is AppStartupInitializer.applyDefaultsChromeOsIfEmpty (AppStartupInitializer.kt:119-121): `if (!bindings.hasOverrides()) { bindings.insertAllAsOverrides(defaultsMapLoader.get().loadChromeOsDefaults()) }` where hasOverrides() is `dao.observeAll().first().isNotEmpty()` (line 53). Concrete failure: process death mid-loop (deferred startup task, freely killable) persists only a prefix of the ChromeOS default bindings; on every next launch hasOverrides() returns true, so the remaining defaults are never applied - a silent, permanent half-configured keymap. Each upsert also invalidates input_bindings, re-running the observeResolvedBindings merge once per row. Violates Layer 4 'multi-step writes that must be atomic are wrapped in @Transaction'.
fix_hint: Make it atomic: a DAO @Insert/@Upsert taking List<InputBindingEntity> (single transaction), or wrap the loop in db.withTransaction.

title: Favorites import inserts row-by-row without a transaction
evidence: In invoke(), the per-entry loop (lines 74-123) executes `favoritesDao.insert(entity)` (line 104) once per imported favorite with no @Transaction/withTransaction around the batch. Each insert is a separate transaction that invalidates the favorites table, so live collectors (FavoritesRepositoryImpl.getAllFavorites feeding the favorites screen, FavoritesDao.getFileFavorites feeding widget/backup consumers) re-query and re-emit once per imported row, and a process kill mid-import commits an arbitrary prefix of the file with no all-or-nothing boundary - the result summary (imported/skipped counts) is then never shown and the user cannot tell what landed. Contrast: the backup-restore path wraps its favorites writes in `db.withTransaction` (ApplyBackupPayloadUseCase.kt:78). Violates Layer 4 'multi-step writes that must be atomic are wrapped in @Transaction'.
fix_hint: Inject AppDatabase and wrap the import loop in db.withTransaction { } (per-entry try/catch can stay - a failed row does not need to abort the batch), matching ApplyBackupPayloadUseCase.

title: ImageReader acquireLatestImage races main-thread close() with no guard - uncaught IllegalStateException on shared HandlerThread kills the process
evidence: Both acquire sites run on the background 'StreamFrameReader' HandlerThread and are NOT protected against the main-thread teardown. Line 215 is outside readFrame's try: `val image = reader.acquireLatestImage() ?: return null` (the `try {` starts only on line 216), and line 147 in the listener is bare: `r.acquireLatestImage()?.close()`. Meanwhile capture()'s finally on the MAIN thread closes the reader with no lock/flag shared with the listener: lines 204-205 `imageReader?.setOnImageAvailableListener(null, null); imageReader?.close()`. ImageReader's ListenerHandler reads the listener reference once at message-dispatch time; a lambda already past that read keeps executing while main runs close(). acquireLatestImage on a closed reader throws IllegalStateException from nativeImageSetup ('ImageReader is not initialized or was already closed') - a well-known field crash signature. Thrown inside the listener lambda it is uncaught (line 147 branch has no try at all; line 215 is before readFrame's try), and an uncaught exception on the companion-object HandlerThread (lines 257-258) is a FATAL EXCEPTION = app crash. Concrete path: capture times out at CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS (line 184-187) or completes on frame 1 while the live decoder (playWhenReady=true, line 182) renders frame 2 during player.release(); the frame message starts executing (listener read pre-line-204), the reader thread is preempted before acquire, main finishes lines 204-205, reader thread resumes into acquireLatestImage on the closed reader. Window is narrow but the operation repeats per visible tile on every 60 s periodic grid refresh, scroll re-capture, and pull-to-refresh.
fix_hint: Guard both acquire sites: move line 215 inside readFrame's try (its catch(Throwable) already returns null) and wrap line 147 in try/catch(IllegalStateException); or share a @Volatile closed flag / lock between the finally and the listener so no acquire can start after close().

title: cancelAll() cannot stop queued captures: drainOne polls the url before suspending on the semaphore, so parked drainOnes launch full ExoPlayer captures after onStop / leaving GRID
evidence: drainOne (lines 102-104): `val url = queue.poll() ?: return` executes BEFORE `semaphore.withPermit {` - the url leaves the queue before the coroutine parks waiting for a permit. With the host's lifecycleScope (Dispatchers.Main.immediate, StreamsActivity:110) every `request()` runs its `scope.launch { drainOne() }` (line 89) synchronously to the first suspension, so with N visible tiles all N urls are polled within milliseconds while only 2 captures hold permits (MAX_CONCURRENT_CAPTURES=2). cancelAll (lines 93-100) then does `queue.clear()` (already empty - no-op), `pending.clear()`, and cancels only `inFlight` - which contains ONLY the launched capture jobs (added at line 112); the N-2 parked drainOne coroutines are tracked nowhere. After cancelAll they acquire freed permits and run `scope.launch { capture(url) }` (line 105) on the still-alive lifecycleScope: each creates an ExoPlayer, opens the network and decodes up to CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS=12 s, two at a time. This directly defeats the documented contract - line 92 'Clear the queue and cancel in-flight captures (leaving GRID / on stop)' and StreamsActivity:736 'S0675: never run frame captures while backgrounded' (onStop:739 calls cancelAll) and StreamGridModeManager:82 (applyMode(LIST) calls cancelAll). Concrete path: GRID with 10 visible video tiles, pull-to-refresh enqueues 10, user presses Home -> onStop -> cancelAll kills 2; the remaining 8 captures run serially in background for up to ~48 s (network + decoder + onOutcome DB writes). Every player is still released in capture's finally, so this is background work after teardown, not a resource leak (P2 per taxonomy: missing lifecycle-awareness without a proven leak).
fix_hint: Poll the url inside withPermit after acquiring, and re-check a generation/cancelled marker after acquire; or track drainOne jobs in inFlight too; or launch all work under a child SupervisorJob that cancelAll cancels and recreates.

title: onComplete is never invoked on cancellation - withContext(Dispatchers.Main) in the finally of a cancelled job throws before running the block, contradicting the KDoc
evidence: Line 67-69: `} finally { withContext(Dispatchers.Main) { onComplete() } }`. When the sweep is cancelled (cancel() line 74-77, wired to onStop and every user interaction in StreamsActivity), the launch's Job is already cancelled when the finally runs; a plain `withContext` in a cancelled coroutine throws CancellationException immediately without executing its block (the documented kotlinx.coroutines behavior that the withContext(NonCancellable) pattern exists for). So onComplete runs only on natural completion, contradicting the KDoc at line 51: '[onComplete] runs on the main thread when the sweep finishes or is cancelled.' Currently latent-only: the sole caller (StreamsActivity:399,401) uses the default `onComplete: () -> Unit = {}`, so no spinner is stuck today - but any future caller relying on the documented contract gets a callback that silently never fires on the most common exit path.
fix_hint: Use `withContext(NonCancellable) { onComplete() }` (the coroutine already runs on the main dispatcher via the host lifecycleScope), or `withContext(Dispatchers.Main + NonCancellable)`.

title: catch (t: Throwable) swallows CancellationException and logs every user-driven sweep cancel as a WARN failure with stack trace
evidence: Lines 118-120: `} catch (t: Throwable) { Timber.w(t, "Stream health probe failed: %s", url); false }`. External cancellation is delivered at `ready.await()` (line 114) as CancellationException and is caught here instead of being rethrown - violating the Layer 2 rule 'cancellation is not swallowed'. Runtime path: a sweep is running and the user scrolls (StreamsActivity:240), types in search (:230), opens filter/sort (:233-234), taps a stream (:443), toggles display mode (:222), or the screen stops (:725) -> cancelHealthProbe -> job.cancel -> CE lands in this catch -> misleading 'Stream health probe failed' WARN + CancellationException stack trace for a normal user action. Status integrity survives only because the loop re-checks `if (!isActive) break` before onStatus (line 64), and the swallowed CE is re-thrown anyway when the enclosing withContext(Dispatchers.Main) completes in the cancelled job.
fix_hint: Add `catch (ce: CancellationException) { throw ce }` before the Throwable catch.

title: catch (t: Throwable) in capture() swallows CancellationException and logs cancelAll-driven cancels as 'Stream snapshot failed' WARNs
evidence: Lines 195-197: `} catch (t: Throwable) { Timber.w(t, "Stream snapshot failed: %s", url); null }`. cancelAll() (onStop, leaving GRID) cancels the in-flight capture jobs; the CancellationException is delivered at `firstFrame.await()` (line 184) and caught here - same 'cancellation is not swallowed' violation as the probe manager, producing up to MAX_CONCURRENT_CAPTURES spurious WARN+stacktrace lines on every screen stop or LIST/GRID toggle while captures are in flight. Harmless functionally (the finally at 198-206 still releases player/surface/reader, and the enclosing withContext rethrows the CE so onCaptured/onOutcome are not invoked for cancelled captures), but it is recurring log noise misreporting normal lifecycle transitions as stream failures.
fix_hint: Add `catch (ce: CancellationException) { throw ce }` before the Throwable catch.

title: Lost-update race between concurrent full-snapshot settings writers in Enable-all deliverable completion (enableOcr/enableTranslation can silently revert)
evidence: enqueueAndEnableOnInstall() launches one appScope coroutine per deliverable set (OCR_ENGINES at line 163, TRANSLATION at line 166): `appScope.launch { val terminal = downloadRunner.progressOf(set).first { ... }; if (terminal is DownloadProgress.Installed) { val current = settingsRepository.getSettings().first(); settingsRepository.updateSettings(enable(current)) } }` (lines 184-191). SettingsRepositoryImpl.updateSettings(settings: AppSettings) (line 527) persists the ENTIRE AppSettings snapshot inside dataStore.edit (line 556); the `getSettings().first()` read happens outside the transaction and the file contains no Mutex/synchronized/withLock. Runtime path: Enable-all enqueues both sets; both coroutines wake on Installed; interleaving D.read -> E.read -> D.write(enableOcr=true) -> E.write(full snapshot built from the pre-D read, i.e. enableOcr=false, enableTranslation=true) silently reverts enableOcr although its engine installed - violating the S0386 enable-only-after-install invariant in the opposite direction (installed but disabled). The same unserialized read-modify-write class is asserted safe by comments that only reduce, not eliminate, the window: ApplyEnableAllSettingsUseCase.kt:21 ('Read-modify-write of the latest snapshot so a concurrent profile/preset write is not clobbered') and WelcomeFunctionalityController.kt:429 ('so concurrent toggle taps do not clobber each other's fields') - two in-flight writers on the multi-threaded @ApplicationScope are not serialized by reading the latest snapshot. Per docs/CODE_AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md Layer 2 ('shared mutable state ... no read-modify-write race') and severity taxonomy P1 ('data race on shared mutable state').
fix_hint: Add a transform-based SettingsRepository.updateSettings((AppSettings)->AppSettings) whose read+fold happens inside dataStore.edit (or serialize all writers behind a repository-level Mutex), then migrate the welcome writers (enqueueAndEnableOnInstall, persist(), applySettingsOnly, ApplyEnableAllSettingsUseCase) to it.

title: Enable-all sequence stalls permanently after recreation/process death: stage-completion callback is instance-bound and restored inProgress=true has no resume path
evidence: runGrantAll(onComplete) stores the enable-all continuation only in the in-memory field `private var grantAllOnComplete: (() -> Unit)? = null` (line 75, set at 169); onSaveInstanceState (lines 140-143) persists grantAllInProgress + shownSpecialInRun but not the stage linkage, and attach() (line 78) never re-arms it. The machinery is explicitly designed to survive recreation (stable registry keys, WelcomePermissionsManager.kt:319-323; state restore, WelcomeEnableAllManager.kt:89-93), and WelcomeActivity is recreatable mid-run despite configChanges=orientation|screenSize|keyboardHidden (AndroidManifest.xml:243 lacks uiMode/smallestScreenSize/screenLayout; process death while the user is on a special-permission system screen is the common case). After recreation the pending special-settings ActivityResult IS delivered to the new instance's callback (stable key KEY_SPECIAL_SETTINGS) and the walk correctly continues on restored state, but at its end `grantAllOnComplete?.invoke()` (line 219) is null on the new instance - so WelcomeEnableAllManager.beginDefaultPlayerStage/finishSequence/onFinished (completeWelcomeFlow) never run, and the new enable-all manager's restored inProgress=true blocks any re-tap forever (`if (inProgress) return`, WelcomeEnableAllManager.kt:98) and is re-saved on every later recreation. Secondary mechanism in the pre-walk window: the appScope coroutine in start() (WelcomeEnableAllManager.kt:105-115) captures the pre-recreation `pm` and manager instances; resumed after a recreation it drives pm.runGrantAll against the DESTROYED Activity (WelcomePermissionsManager.activity is never cleared - no detach exists) and its dead ActivityResultRegistry launchers, and the final finishSequence invokes completeWelcomeFlow/finish() on the destroyed instance while the visible instance never advances. Failure scenario: tap 'Enable all' -> OS opens the MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE settings screen -> process is killed in background (or auto dark-mode flips uiMode) -> user returns: permissions finish, but onboarding never completes and the Enable-all button stays dead for the session. No crash/leak proof, so P2 (missing lifecycle-awareness / broken cross-recreation state machine).
fix_hint: Persist the stage in the Bundle and rebuild the linkage on restore: in WelcomeEnableAllManager.attach(), when restored inProgress==true, re-arm permissionsManager.grantAllOnComplete (and resume the correct stage); resolve activity/pm at resume time instead of capturing them in the appScope closure; clear WelcomePermissionsManager.activity/binding on host destroy.

title: Type-gated releaseActiveViewer() lets an in-flight async load of the previous document type resurrect PdfRenderer/PFD/WebView that no teardown path ever releases
evidence: releaseActiveViewer() releases only the viewer of the current resolvedType: `when (resolvedType) { MediaType.PDF -> pdfViewerManager.close(); MediaType.EPUB -> epubViewerManager.release(); MediaType.OFFICE_DOCUMENT -> if (officeViewerHostDelegate.isInitialized()) { officeViewerHost.release() }; else -> Unit }` (lines 792-803), and the paging swap runs it before switching type: `if (lastShownPath != null) releaseActiveViewer(); resolvedType = type; displayDocument(file, type)` (lines 709-711). The viewers' display entry points are unguarded async coroutines on lifecycleScope: PdfViewerManager.displayPdf launches `coroutineScope.launch(Dispatchers.Main) { kotlinx.coroutines.delay(50); ... pdfParcelFileDescriptor = ParcelFileDescriptor.open(file, ...); pdfRenderer = PdfRenderer(pdfParcelFileDescriptor!!)` (PdfViewerManager.kt:316-353) with no cancellation or current-file generation check; EpubViewerManager.displayEpub likewise delays 50ms then getOrCreateWebView() re-creates the WebView (EpubViewerManager.kt:333-335, 480; EpubWebViewLifecycle.getOrCreate():29-43); openOfficeInternally calls `officeViewerHost.open(...)` only after suspending prepareFileForRead (lines 750-755), so at swap time officeViewerHostDelegate.isInitialized() is still false and the release is skipped. CONCRETE PATH: folder-paged mixed-type docs (host supports PDF+EPUB+OFFICE neighbours, line 681) - user opens a PDF and taps Next onto an EPUB neighbour within the load window (guaranteed >=50ms + IO prepare + renderer open; seconds for SMB/cloud). releaseActiveViewer() runs while pdfRenderer is still null (no-op), resolvedType becomes EPUB, then the stale coroutine resumes: opens a new ParcelFileDescriptor + PdfRenderer and renders a 2x-screen ARGB_8888 bitmap (up to 2560px, ~25MB) into photoView over the EPUB. Neither a later swap nor onDestroy calls pdfViewerManager.close() again (resolvedType != PDF), so the native renderer, fd (CloseGuard 'PFD leaked') and bitmap outlive teardown. Symmetric: EPUB->PDF resurrects a destroyed WebView; noLegal Office->other leaves an undestroyed office WebView with officeDocumentViewerContainer visible. Contrast the family contract: the unified host releases EVERY initialized manager unconditionally - `if (activity._epubViewerManager != null) activity.epubViewerManager.release(); if (activity._officeDocumentViewerManager != null) ...release(); if (activity._pdfViewerManager != null) activity.pdfViewerManager.close()` (PlayerLifecycleManager.kt:247-253); StandaloneViewManager.release() does `_pdfViewerManager?.close(); _epubViewerManager?.release(); _textViewerManager?.release()` (StandaloneViewManager.kt:328-333).
fix_hint: Make onDestroy/releaseActiveViewer release every initialized viewer (nullable backing or lazy-delegate isInitialized() checks, as already done for officeViewerHostDelegate), and/or add a load-generation guard inside displayPdf/displayEpub/openOfficeInternally that aborts a stale load after each suspension point.

title: onDestroy never releases TranslationManager - ML Kit Translator native model and offline OCR engines stay open after PDF/EPUB translation/OCR use
evidence: onDestroy() is only `releaseActiveViewer(); super.onDestroy()` (lines 786-789). The activity owns `private val translationManager: TranslationManager by lazy { TranslationManager(...) }` (lines 170-193), forced whenever pdfViewerManager/epubViewerManager is built (ctor args, lines 295, 320), and translation/OCR are first-class wired features here (btnTranslatePdfCmd:604, btnOcrPdfCmd:608, btnTranslateEpubCmd:629, btnOcrEpubCmd:627). TranslationManager.release() exists and frees heavy natives: `recognitionBackend.release(); translationBackend.release()` (TranslationManager.kt:410-413) -> `translator?.close()` on the ML Kit Translator holding a loaded translation model (TranslationBackend.kt:289-292) and `offlineOcrEngineProvider.release()` (RecognitionBackend.kt:243-245). Neither PdfViewerManager.close() (lines 684-711) nor EpubViewerManager.release() (lines 636-640) calls it, and the only call site in the whole player package is the unified host: `activity.translationManager.release()` (PlayerLifecycleManager.kt:262-267). RUNTIME PATH: user opens a PDF from an external app, taps translate/OCR (Translator created, model loaded into native memory), closes the activity - onDestroy releases only the PDF viewer, translator.close() never runs, and the loaded model plus any initialized offline OCR engine remain resident until non-deterministic finalization, repeated per session. Violates the Layer-3 mirrored-host rule (same release contract in every host).
fix_hint: Track initialization (convert to `private val translationManagerDelegate = lazy { ... }` - the pattern already used for officeViewerHostDelegate at line 327) and call `if (translationManagerDelegate.isInitialized()) translationManager.release()` in onDestroy before super.

title: onDestroy never releases TranslationManager - text-translation ML Kit Translator left unclosed on teardown
evidence: onDestroy() is only `textViewerManager.release(); super.onDestroy()` (lines 548-551). The activity owns `private val translationManager: TranslationManager by lazy { ... }` (lines 205-228), forced by textViewerManager construction (ctor arg, line 248) which setupViews always triggers via `textViewerManager.setupControls()` (line 296). RUNTIME PATH: user opens a .txt from another app, taps the translate button (Translator created, model loaded natively), finishes the activity - the translator is never closed, leaving the model resident in native memory until GC finalization, accumulating across repeated standalone text sessions.
fix_hint: Mirror the unified host: lazy delegate + isInitialized() guard, then translationManager.release() in onDestroy when built.

title: onDestroy force-initializes the entire lazy TextViewerManager graph when the activity dies before deferred setupViews() ran
evidence: `override fun onDestroy() { textViewerManager.release(); super.onDestroy() }` (lines 548-551) dereferences the `by lazy` textViewerManager unconditionally. BaseActivity defers setupViews() to `binding.root.post { if (_binding == null || isDestroyed) return@post; setupViews() ... }` (BaseActivity.kt:145-160), so an activity finished within the first frame (immediate back-press or upstream finish) reaches onDestroy with the lazy untouched; the release call then constructs TextViewerManager plus its ctor-arg lazies (TranslationManager, NetworkFileManager, TextEditorSaveFlow) and starts the dirty-tracker collector (`.also { it.start(coroutineScope) }`, TextViewerManager.kt:131-134) during teardown, purely to release nothing - wasted allocations and a transient coroutine on a dying scope; no leak.
