title: MediaPlayer fallback never stops or releases the still-playing ExoPlayer - two concurrent active players
evidence: playWithMediaPlayer() (lines 115-127) does: `cancelPlaybackHealthCheck(); isUsingMediaPlayer = true; releaseMediaPlayer(); mediaPlayer = MediaPlayer().apply { .. prepareAsync() }` - it never pauses, stops, or releases manager.exoPlayer. Its health-check trigger guarantees the ExoPlayer is actively playing at that moment: checkPlaybackHealth() line 56 `if (!player.isPlaying || player.playbackState != Player.STATE_READY) { .. return }` and line 73-81 posts `playWithMediaPlayer(currentFilePath!!)` only after two stuck polls. Runtime path: play a local FLAC/AC3/EAC3/WV file whose decode is stuck emitting white noise -> after 2 polls (~4 s) the fallback MediaPlayer starts() in onPrepared while the ExoPlayer keeps decoding and outputting white noise (it also still holds audio focus via handleAudioFocus=true, which MediaPlayer never requests). Result: two live decoders and doubled audible output until the next releasePlayer()/onDestroy. Violates contract items 1 (one active player) and 7 (failure path releases too).
fix_hint: In playWithMediaPlayer(), stop and release (or at minimum pause+stop) the ExoPlayer before starting MediaPlayer, e.g. exoPlayer?.stop() plus releasePlayer()-style teardown of the exo instance while keeping currentFilePath state.

title: isUsingMediaPlayer set-then-reset ordering bug: releaseMediaPlayer() clears the flag, so the fallback MediaPlayer is uncontrollable and keeps playing in background
evidence: Lines 118-119: `isUsingMediaPlayer = true` then `releaseMediaPlayer()`; releaseMediaPlayer() line 187-188 unconditionally ends with `mediaPlayer = null; isUsingMediaPlayer = false` and the flag is never set true again after the new MediaPlayer is created. All routing reads this flag: VideoPlaybackControlsHelper.pause() lines 111-118 `if (manager.isUsingMediaPlayer) { .. mediaPlayer?.pause() } else { manager.exoPlayer?.pause() }`, play() line 121, and the lifecycle edge VideoPlayerLifecycleHelper.onPause() lines 55-58 `wasPlayingBeforePause = manager.exoPlayer?.isPlaying == true || (manager.isUsingMediaPlayer && manager.mediaPlayer?.isPlaying == true); manager.pause()`. Runtime path: after the white-noise fallback engages, the user presses pause or backgrounds the activity (ON_PAUSE) -> pause() routes to exoPlayer only, mediaPlayer keeps playing audio with the screen off/app in background until Activity onDestroy finally releases mediaPlayerToRelease (VideoPlayerLifecycleHelper.kt:110-122). Also breaks playVideo()'s `!isUsingMediaPlayer` position-restore guard.
fix_hint: Reorder: call releaseMediaPlayer() first, then set isUsingMediaPlayer = true after constructing the new MediaPlayer (or make releaseMediaPlayer() not touch the flag and set it explicitly at both call sites).

title: Entering Picture-in-Picture pauses video: manager-level ON_PAUSE handler lacks the PiP guard the Activity has
evidence: VideoPlayerManager is a DefaultLifecycleObserver on the Activity lifecycle (VideoPlayerManager.kt:562-564 `lifecycle.addObserver(this)`, PlayerViewerFactory.kt:15 `lifecycle = activity.lifecycle`) and its onPause (VideoPlayerManager.kt:779) delegates unconditionally to onPause() here, lines 52-59: `manager.flushWatchClock(); wasPlayingBeforePause = ..; manager.pause(); manager.stopPositionSaving()`. PlayerActivity.onPause() deliberately skips its own pause work in PiP - PlayerActivity.kt:963-966 `super.onPause(); if (isInPictureInPictureMode) return` - but super.onPause() already dispatched ON_PAUSE to all lifecycle observers, so the player is paused anyway. PictureInPictureManager.onPictureInPictureModeChanged(true) (PictureInPictureManager.kt:101-119) only hides chrome/registers the receiver and never resumes. Runtime path: video playing -> PiP button or auto-enter on home (API 31+) -> activity enters PiP paused state -> ON_PAUSE dispatch pauses ExoPlayer -> PiP window shows a frozen frame until the user taps the remote PLAY action; position auto-save also stops while PiP is 'playing'.
fix_hint: Gate the manager pause on PiP, e.g. route through the host (PlayerCallback) with an isInPictureInPictureMode check, or move the pause to ON_STOP which does not fire while in PiP.

title: releasePlayer() releases the ExoPlayer while it is still attached to PlayerView - no setVideoSurface(null)/player detach before release (asymmetric with onDestroy)
evidence: releasePlayer() lines 33-38: `manager.exoPlayer?.let { player -> player.removeListener(manager.playerListener); player.release(); manager.exoPlayer = null }` - there is no `currentPlayerView?.player = null` or clearVideoSurface() before release(), and currentPlayerView keeps referencing the released instance afterwards. The destroy path does it correctly and in the right order: onDestroy() lines 84-92 removes the listener then `manager.currentPlayerView?.player = null` BEFORE `playerToRelease?.release()` (line 105). The project itself documents why surface detach before/at release matters on this codec stack: PlayerActivityLifecycleBridge.kt:60 'Without this CCodec keeps the Surface alive across ATMS window transition (permanent black screen..)'. Runtime path: switching video -> image/PDF (PlayerLifecycleManager.stopVideoPlayback() lines 627-634 -> pause()+releasePlayer()), the periodic recreate (VideoPlaybackPreflightHelper.kt:98-102), and every protocol-swap releasePlayer() all release with the surface still attached. Violates contract item 3.
fix_hint: In releasePlayer(), detach first: `manager.currentPlayerView?.player = null` (or player.clearVideoSurface()) before removeListener/release, mirroring onDestroy().

title: Orphan creation path: releaseResources() constructs a brand-new VideoPlayerManager during Activity.onDestroy when none exists (dead catch never fires)
evidence: Lines 226-230: `try { activity.videoPlayerManager.releasePlayer() } catch (e: UninitializedPropertyAccessException) { // Not initialized, skip }`. But videoPlayerManager is not lateinit - it is a lazily-creating getter, PlayerActivity.kt:132-134: `internal val videoPlayerManager: VideoPlayerManager get() = _videoPlayerManager ?: PlayerViewerFactory(this).createVideoPlayerManager().also { _videoPlayerManager = it }` - so the catch is dead code and the intended skip never happens. Runtime path: any player session that never played video/audio in-app (image, PDF, text - _videoPlayerManager == null) -> PlayerActivity.onDestroy() (line 1028) -> releaseResources() -> the getter builds a full VideoPlayerManager mid-teardown: its init registers a lifecycle observer (VideoPlayerManager.kt:562-564) and launches two settings collectors in managerScope (VideoPlayerManager.kt:373-398), then releasePlayer() immediately early-returns (VideoPlayerLifecycleHelper.kt:21). Cleanup only happens because super.onDestroy() later dispatches ON_DESTROY to the just-added observer. Wasteful construction plus observer registration on every non-video session teardown; contract item 1 (no orphan creation path). PlayerActivity.releasePlayer() (line 935-937) shows the correct `_videoPlayerManager != null` guard.
fix_hint: Use the null-safe backing field: `activity._videoPlayerManager?.releasePlayer()` and delete the dead catch.

title: Only playerListener is removed at release - PauseAwareLoadControl and the per-stream listener are never removed
evidence: Both release paths remove exactly one listener: line 34 and line 84 `player.removeListener(manager.playerListener)`. But creation paths add more Player.Listeners: PlayerSetupHelper.kt:51-52 `player.addListener(playerListener); player.addListener(loadControl)` (PauseAwareLoadControl implements Player.Listener, PauseAwareLoadControl.kt:22-24), same pattern at CloudPlaybackHelper.kt:74, SmbPlaybackHelper.kt:123, SftpPlaybackHelper.kt:118, FtpPlaybackHelper.kt:109, and StreamPlaybackHelper.kt:80 adds `streamPlaybackListener(path)` (which is never referenced again, so it cannot be removed). Impact is contained because every such player instance is released and dropped immediately after (listeners become unreachable with it), but the contract item 4 requirement 'EVERY added Player.Listener removed before or at release' is not met and the asymmetry invites bugs if an instance is ever reused.
fix_hint: Track secondary listeners on the manager (e.g. activeExtraListeners list populated at each addListener site) and remove them in releasePlayer()/onDestroy() before release().

title: releasePlayer() does not stop the positionSaveLoop - idle 15 s Handler tick survives video-to-document switches
evidence: releasePlayer() (lines 20-50) cancels effects runnables, health check, throttle mode, and retry runnable but never calls stopPositionSaving(); onPause() (line 58), onDestroy() (line 75) and the next-file preflight (VideoPlaybackPreflightHelper.kt:92) all do. Runtime path: video playing -> user opens a PDF/EPUB/text file in the same player -> PlayerLifecycleManager.stopVideoPlayback() (lines 627-634) calls videoPlayerManager.pause() + releasePlayer() -> PositionSaveLoop keeps re-posting every 15 s (PositionSaveLoop.kt:36-39) with exoPlayer == null; each tick no-ops via the `duration <= 0` guard (PositionSaveLoop.kt:60) but the Handler loop runs until the next video load, activity pause, or destroy. Asymmetric teardown (contract item 8), harmless but pointless wakeups.
fix_hint: Add manager.stopPositionSaving() to releasePlayer() alongside cancelPlaybackHealthCheck().

title: BD-TS local path builds ExoPlayer inline, skipping createPlayer() bookkeeping (duplicate creation path)
evidence: Lines 93-108: for non-standard TS packets the helper does `releasePlayer(); .. exoPlayer = ExoPlayer.Builder(context).setMediaSourceFactory(..).setAudioAttributes(audioAttr, true).build(); exoPlayer?.addListener(playerListener); currentPlayerView?.player = exoPlayer` - a second, inline creation path that bypasses createPlayer() (PlayerSetupHelper.kt:28-76). Concretely skipped bookkeeping: `effectsPipelineActive = false` reset (stale true from the previous instance defeats the empty-effects skip guard in applyConfiguredVideoEffects, PlayerSetupHelper.kt:97), applyConfiguredVideoEffects() re-application, and the `onPlayerCreated?.invoke(player)` notification the VR flavor relies on to flush a pending surface redirect (VideoPlayerManager.kt:411-416). releasePlayer()-first, playerListener and audio focus are all correct, so ownership stays single, but the paths diverge on instance-reset semantics. Contract item 1 (no duplicate creation path).
fix_hint: Extend createPlayer() with an optional MediaSourceFactory parameter (or a creation lambda) and route the BD-TS branch through it so all instance-reset bookkeeping stays in one place.

title: Restart during async save orphans an active MediaRecorder (mic stays on); onDestroy never releases recorder or audio focus
evidence: stopAndSave() flips all state to idle BEFORE the suspend save finishes: `releaseRecorder(); abandonFocus(); isRecording = false; QuickAudioRecorderWidgetProvider.updateAllWidgets(this, false)` (lines 140-143), then launches `serviceScope.launch { micRecordingSaver.save(... upload = { ... uploadToResource ... }) ... stopForegroundCompat(); stopSelf() }` (lines 148-173) - the upload path goes through LocalToFtp/Smb/Sftp/cloud strategies, so this window lasts seconds. During it a widget tap re-enters onStartCommand -> handleStart(); the only guard is `if (isRecording) return` (line 84), which is now false, so a NEW MediaRecorder is created and started (lines 100-119, isRecording=true). When the first save completes, its coroutine unconditionally calls `stopSelf()` (line 172; no-arg stopSelf ignores newer startIds) -> onDestroy runs, which is only `serviceScope.cancel(); super.onDestroy()` (lines 200-203) - no releaseRecorder(), no abandonFocus(). The second session's native MediaRecorder keeps capturing the microphone with no owner: the static `isRecording` stays true, and the next ACTION_STOP spawns a fresh service instance whose `mediaRecorder` is null and `recorderStarted` false, so stopAndSave() releases nothing and just toasts an error. Result: microphone + audio focus held until process death, second recording lost. Violates protocol Layer 3 'player instances are always released' / P1 'unreleased heavy resource'.
fix_hint: Guard handleStart() with an isFinalizing/save-in-progress flag (or use stopSelf(startId)), and make onDestroy() call releaseRecorder() + abandonFocus() and reset the static isRecording as a last-resort teardown.

title: isFinalizing latch is never reset - a recording started during finalization cannot be stopped and is silently killed and stranded
evidence: `private var isFinalizing = false` (line 82) is set true in stopAndSave() (line 179) and never reset anywhere in the file. stopAndSave() sets `isRecording = false` (line 193) then launches `serviceScope.launch { saveRecording(tempFile) }` (line 204). While that save copies the (potentially large) MP4, onStartCommand's only re-entry guard is `if (isRecording) return START_NOT_STICKY` (line 99), so a second consent flow starts a full new projection+recorder session. During this window the notification Stop action is dead: `private fun stopAndSave() { if (isFinalizing) return ... }` (lines 177-179). saveRecording()'s finally then executes `pendingTempFile = null` (line 223), discarding the reference to the SECOND session's file, and finishService() calls `stopSelf()` (lines 328-331) -> onDestroy stops the second recorder via `runCatching { mediaRecorder?.stop() }` and releases resources (lines 104-116), but `pendingTempFile?.delete()` is a no-op on null - the second recording is silently terminated mid-capture and its .mp4 stays stranded in the Movies temp dir, never saved and never cleaned.
fix_hint: Reset isFinalizing (and reject new starts) around the finalize window: either set isFinalizing=false when the save completes and guard startRecording() with it, or key stopAndSave() re-entrancy per session instead of a one-way latch.

title: MediaController built asynchronously can land after onStopListening; next listen cycle overwrites it without release, leaking the controller and its Player.Listener
evidence: connectToSession() resolves the controller asynchronously: `val future = MediaController.Builder(this, token).buildAsync(); future.addListener({ ... mediaController = future.get(); mediaController?.addListener(tilePlayerListener) ... }, MoreExecutors.directExecutor())` (lines 75-86). onStopListening() calls releaseController() (lines 38-41), but if the QS panel is closed before the future completes, releaseController() sees `mediaController == null` and does nothing; the callback then assigns the connected controller and attaches tilePlayerListener AFTER the tile stopped listening. On the next panel open, onStartListening() -> connectToSession() runs again and the callback overwrites `mediaController = future.get()` (line 78) - the previous connected instance is never removeListener'd nor release()'d. Each iteration of this open/close race leaks one MediaController binder connection to AudioPlaybackService with a live Player.Listener that keeps mutating the tile; only process death cleans it up. Violates listener-symmetry / 'one owner per player-facing resource'.
fix_hint: In the buildAsync callback, if the tile is no longer listening (or mediaController already set), release the freshly built controller immediately; also release any existing controller at the top of connectToSession().

title: MediaExtractor released only inside the use-block happy path - leaks native extractor when openFileDescriptor returns null or setDataSource/getTrackFormat throws
evidence: extractVideoAudioInfo() creates the extractor before the descriptor: `val extractor = MediaExtractor(); context.contentResolver.openFileDescriptor(uri, "r")?.use { pfd -> extractor.setDataSource(pfd.fileDescriptor); ... extractor.release() }` with only `catch (e: Exception) { Timber.w(e, "MediaExtractor failed for SAF URI, using basic metadata only") }` around it (lines 145-176). `extractor.release()` (line 172) is the last statement of the use-block, so (1) if openFileDescriptor returns null the block never runs and the extractor is never released, and (2) if setDataSource or getTrackFormat throws (corrupt/truncated file, revoked SAF grant - the exact case this catch anticipates), the exception skips release(). The enclosing finally (line 196-198) releases only the retriever. Every failed SAF video/audio probe leaks one native MediaExtractor. The sibling MediaMetadataHelper was already fixed for this exact defect class - its finally comments 'Release native MediaExtractor on every path, incl. throws from setDataSource/getTrackFormat (S0726/S0715 P2)' (MediaMetadataHelper.kt:379-381) - SafUriExtractor never got the fix.
fix_hint: Mirror MediaMetadataHelper: move MediaExtractor creation inside a try with `finally { extractor.release() }`, or create it only after a non-null pfd and wrap the whole use-block body.

title: extractPdfInfo leaks the ParcelFileDescriptor when the PdfRenderer constructor throws (corrupt or password-protected PDF)
evidence: `val pfd = context.contentResolver.openFileDescriptor(uri, "r"); if (pfd != null) { val pdfRenderer = android.graphics.pdf.PdfRenderer(pfd); val count = pdfRenderer.pageCount; pdfRenderer.close(); pfd.close(); count } else null` wrapped only in `catch (e: Exception) { Timber.w(...); null }` (lines 211-223). Both closes are on the happy path with no finally: PdfRenderer's constructor throws SecurityException for password-protected PDFs and IOException for corrupt ones without closing the descriptor, so the catch swallows the exception and the open ParcelFileDescriptor is abandoned until its CloseGuard finalizer. File-info on any protected/corrupt SAF PDF leaks an fd per call. Violates protocol Layer 3 'resource closure is enforced using .use { } for all Closeable types' (ThumbnailExtractorHelper.extractPdfThumbnail lines 159-163 shows the correct finally-based pattern in the same codebase).
fix_hint: Wrap pfd/pdfRenderer in `pfd.use { PdfRenderer(it).use { r -> r.pageCount } }` or a try/finally closing both.

title: remux() leaks a native MediaExtractor when setDataSource fails on a segment file
evidence: Per segment: `val extractor = MediaExtractor(); try { extractor.setDataSource(segment.absolutePath) } catch (t: Throwable) { return RemuxResult.MuxFailed(codec = "extractor_failed:${segment.name}") }` (lines 54-59). The release finally (`finally { runCatching { extractor.release() } }`, lines 123-125) belongs to the SECOND try block starting at line 60, so the early return at line 58 exits remux() with the freshly created extractor never released; the outer finally (lines 138-143) releases only the muxer. Trigger: a truncated/corrupt downloaded HLS/DASH segment (the exact failure this catch handles) leaks one native MediaExtractor per remux attempt. Same defect class as the S0726/S0715 P2 fix applied to MediaMetadataHelper.
fix_hint: Fold setDataSource into the second try so the existing `finally { extractor.release() }` covers it, e.g. create the extractor, then one try { setDataSource(...); ... } finally { release() } with the MuxFailed return inside.

title: startPositionSaving() overwrites the previous PositionSaveLoop without stop() - orphaned self-reposting Handler runnable retains PlayerActivity forever after destroy
evidence: PlaybackPositionHelper.kt:22-41: 'internal fun VideoPlayerManager.startPositionSaving() { positionSaveLoop = PositionSaveLoop(...); positionSaveLoop!!.start() }' - the old loop instance is overwritten, never stopped (KDoc claims "Replaces any previously scheduled save loop" but only the reference is replaced). PositionSaveLoop.start() stops only its own runnable, and the runnable self-reposts unconditionally: PositionSaveLoop.kt:36-38 'override fun run() { saveNow(); handler.postDelayed(this, intervalMs) }'. The sequential path is guarded only because VideoPlaybackPreflightHelper.runPreflight (called synchronously at playVideo entry) does manager.stopPositionSaving() at line 92; but playVideo launches an un-serialized coroutine per call (VideoPlayerManager.kt:620 'managerScope.launch {' with no previous-job cancel) that suspends at least at playbackPositionRepository.getPosition(path) (:622) and credentialsRepository.getByCredentialId (helpers) before reaching startPositionSaving() (:671). If playVideo(B) is dispatched while coroutine A is still in flight, both preflights run before either startPositionSaving(); the second startPositionSaving() then orphans the first loop. Nothing can ever stop the orphan: stopPositionSaving/onPause/onDestroy touch only the current positionSaveLoop (VideoPlayerLifecycleHelper.kt:75), and managerScope.cancel() at onDestroy (:125) does not affect the Handler chain (Handler-based, not coroutine-based). The loop lambdas capture the VideoPlayerManager ('getPath = { currentFilePath }', 'getPositionMs = { exoPlayer?.currentPosition ... }'), and VideoPlayerManager holds 'context = activity' and playerCallback = PlayerPlaybackCallbackImpl(activity = activity, ...) (PlayerViewerFactory.kt:14-17), so the main Looper permanently retains the destroyed PlayerActivity plus its PlayerView, and ticks a runnable every 15 s for the rest of the process lifetime (one more per race occurrence).
fix_hint: Make startPositionSaving() call stopPositionSaving() (or positionSaveLoop?.stop()) before creating the new loop, and/or serialize playVideo by cancelling the previous load job; also stop the loop in releasePlayer().

title: Duplicate-player race: network TS-probe suspension between releasePlayer() and exoPlayer assignment lets an interleaved load orphan a prepared, playing ExoPlayer (never released)
evidence: FtpPlaybackHelper.kt:46 'releasePlayer()' ... :95-99 'val format = if (routeHint == NetworkPlaybackContainerHint.M2TS_TS_CANDIDATE) { (dataSourceFactory as DataSource.Factory).detectTsFormatSuspend(ftpUri) }' ... :101 'exoPlayer = ExoPlayer.Builder(context)...'. detectTsFormatSuspend is a real suspension doing network I/O (BdTsPlaybackHelper.kt:39-63: withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { source.open(spec); source.read(...) } over FTP/SMB/SFTP/cloud - seconds on a slow link). The same release->suspend->assign window exists in SftpPlaybackHelper.kt:43/:104-110, SmbPlaybackHelper.kt:44/:108-115 and CloudPlaybackHelper.kt:35/:60-66. playVideo dispatches each request as an independent managerScope coroutine with no cancellation of the previous one (VideoPlayerManager.kt:620-683; managerScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Main + Job()) at :337), and PlayerMediaLoaderManager.playVideoWithResourceType calls videoPlayerManager.playVideo per file display with no serialization (:1049-1112). Concrete interleaving: user opens network file A ('.m2ts'/'.m2t' per NetworkPlaybackContainerHint.fromPath) -> coroutine A passes releasePlayer() and suspends in detectTsFormatSuspend -> user swipes to file B -> coroutine B's releasePlayer() finds exoPlayer == null (releases nothing), builds player PB, prepares and plays it -> coroutine A resumes and executes 'exoPlayer = PA', 'currentPlayerView?.player = PA'. PB is now unreachable and is NEVER released: it keeps playing file B's audio (double audio, no surface), holds MediaCodec decoders, its buffered data and its pooled FTP/SMB/SFTP connection (semaphore permit) until the process dies, while the stale file A wins the screen.
fix_hint: Track the in-flight load Job in VideoPlayerManager and cancel it at playVideo entry (or guard with a Mutex), and/or re-check-and-release any existing exoPlayer at the assignment point after suspension.

title: Stream error-recovery jobs (up to 5 s / 16 s delayed) act on whatever exoPlayer is current, not the errored instance - yanks the next file's restored position
evidence: StreamPlaybackHelper.kt:183-187 (BehindLiveWindow branch): 'managerScope.launch { delay(backoffMs); exoPlayer?.seekToDefaultPosition(); exoPlayer?.prepare() }' and :199-203 (transient branch): 'managerScope.launch { delay(backoffMs); if (!isRtsp && exoPlayer?.isCurrentMediaItemLive == true) exoPlayer?.seekToDefaultPosition(); exoPlayer?.prepare() }'. The lambdas read the manager field 'exoPlayer', not the player the listener was attached to; backoff reaches 5 s (behind-live) and 16 s (STREAM_TRANSIENT_BASE_DELAY_MS shl 3, :197/:267-269). managerScope is cancelled only at onDestroy (VideoPlayerLifecycleHelper.kt:125), and releasePlayer() does not cancel these jobs. Runtime path: live stream errors with BEHIND_LIVE_WINDOW -> recovery job scheduled -> within the backoff the user switches to another file -> releasePlayer() + new player created and its saved position restored (VideoPlayerManager.kt:659-669 'exoPlayer?.seekTo(savedPosition)') -> the stale job fires and calls seekToDefaultPosition() on the NEW player, discarding the restored position (VOD jumps to its default start); prepare() is a no-op unless IDLE but the seek is user-visible.
fix_hint: Capture the player instance in the listener closure and guard the delayed block with 'if (exoPlayer !== erroredPlayer) return@launch', or cancel pending recovery jobs in releasePlayer().

title: Player never released on the background edge - onPause only pauses, no onStop release/onStart recreate, so codecs + buffered media are retained while the app is backgrounded
evidence: VideoPlayerLifecycleHelper.kt:52-59: 'fun onPause() { manager.flushWatchClock(); wasPlayingBeforePause = manager.exoPlayer?.isPlaying == true ...; manager.pause(); manager.stopPositionSaving() }' - the ExoPlayer instance is kept; the class defines no onStop handler and VideoPlayerManager overrides only onPause/onResume/onDestroy (VideoPlayerManager.kt:779-786). Release happens only on destroy, explicit swap (helpers/stopVideoPlayback) or periodic recreation. This deviates from the release contract edge (protocol Layer 3: 'release on onStop for API 24+ multi-window, re-create on onStart') and from CLAUDE.md Rule 18 ('release player/media resources immediately when paused') with no documenting comment for the alternative. Runtime path: user home-presses during network video playback -> activity stopped indefinitely -> MediaCodec decoders plus up to maxBufferMs of buffered media (45 s cloud, 60 s VOD-stream ceiling per BandwidthAdaptiveLoadControl) stay allocated in the background; PauseAwareLoadControl only stops further loading (returns false from shouldContinueLoading when !playWhenReady), it does not free what is buffered.
fix_hint: Release in onStop and rebuild/restore in onStart (position is already persisted via saveCurrentPosition/PositionSaveLoop), or document the keep-alive as the deliberate multi-window/PiP decision at the onPause site.

title: releasePlayer() (swap edge) releases without setVideoSurface(null)/PlayerView detach - released player stays attached to PlayerView until the next attach or destroy
evidence: VideoPlayerLifecycleHelper.kt:33-38: 'manager.exoPlayer?.let { player -> player.removeListener(manager.playerListener); player.release(); manager.exoPlayer = null }' - no clearVideoSurface/setVideoSurface(null) and no 'currentPlayerView?.player = null' before release, unlike onDestroy which correctly detaches first (:89 'manager.currentPlayerView?.player = null' then :105 'playerToRelease?.release()'). Contract item 3 requires the surface detach before release on video hosts. Runtime path: switching from a video to an image (PlayerLifecycleManager.stopVideoPlayback:627-634 pause + releasePlayer) leaves binding.playerView.player referencing the released ExoPlayer until onDestroy or the next video attach; PlayerView keeps interacting with a released Player instance.
fix_hint: In releasePlayer(), detach first: currentPlayerView?.player = null (or player.clearVideoSurface()) before player.release(), mirroring onDestroy().

title: Idle-pool machinery is dead code: connectionPool is never populated, so cleanupIdleFtpConnections() is a permanent no-op that FtpClient still arms on every acquire

title: Crash: candidateFiles.random() on empty list when the playlist's only track is marked failed (IO-error skip path is uncaught)
evidence: Line 407: `val randomFile = candidateFiles.random()`. For a single-file playlist the branch at line 391 (`if (availableAudioFiles.size > 1 && currentTrackPath != null)`) is false, so line 404 runs: `availableAudioFiles.filter { it.path !in failedFiles }` - empty once that one file is in failedFiles - and `random()` on an empty collection throws NoSuchElementException. title: Data race: failedFiles/currentTrackPath/availableAudioFiles/isPlaying/loadPlaylistJob mutated from both main thread and Dispatchers.IO workers with no synchronization
evidence: Unguarded fields: `private val failedFiles = mutableSetOf<String>()` (line 51), `currentTrackPath` (47), `availableAudioFiles` (46), `currentTrackName` (48), `isPlaying` (41), `loadPlaylistJob` (67) - no Mutex/@Volatile/thread confinement. fix_hint: Confine all state mutation to the main thread (hop to Dispatchers.Main before touching manager state in skipToNextRandomTrack/loadAndSetPlaylist, keep only the download on IO), or guard the fields with a Mutex.

title: Multi-window: first-destroyed PlayerActivity releases the shared singleton player out from under the surviving window and permanently unhooks its UI listeners (contract item 1: host ownership not exclusive)
evidence: `@Singleton` (line 32) means ALL PlayerActivity instances share one manager + one player, and duplicate live windows are by design: PlayerActivity.tearOffPlayer() (PlayerActivity.kt:822-835, comment "S0184: open a duplicate Player in a new window slot while keeping the source player alive") launches with FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK|FLAG_ACTIVITY_MULTIPLE_TASK (also BrowseEventHandler.kt:287-288); the manifest declares no launchMode (AndroidManifest.xml:212). Runtime path with windows A (slideshow + music playing) and B: (a) B's own state collector (PlayerObserverManager.kt:44-48) calls updateState(B.state); with B not music-eligible the else-branch (lines 202-215) runs `loadPlaylistJob?.cancel()` and `musicPlayer?.clearMediaItems()` (209) - killing A's playing music deterministically; (b) closing B runs PlayerLifecycleManager.kt:186-188 `backgroundMusicManager.release()` -> player released and `onTrackChangedListener = null; onMusicErrorListener = null` (lines 551-552) while A still lives; A's `areAudioBackgroundManagersConfigured` flag is already true so ensureAudioBackgroundManagersConfigured() early-returns (PlayerManagerInitializer.kt:171-173) and never re-wires the listeners -> A's track-name display and error toasts are dead for the rest of its life (music itself lazily re-creates a player via line 231 on A's next eligible state). Duplicate/orphan creation was verified absent (all creation funnels through the null-guarded main-thread initializeInternal, line 96; post-release recovery coroutines are inert because release() empties availableAudioFiles at 546 so skip early-returns at 383), so the defect is host-ownership, not instance duplication.
fix_hint: Refcount configured hosts and release only when the last one is destroyed, or scope the manager to the activity (remove @Singleton) since all state is per-session anyway; at minimum re-wire listeners on window resume.

title: No audio-focus handling: player built without setAudioAttributes(attrs, handleAudioFocus=true), unlike every other player host in the app (contract item 5, acquisition half)

Every other ExoPlayer host sets it: PlayerSetupHelper.kt:48 `.setAudioAttributes(audioAttributes, true) // handleAudioFocus=true`, AudioPlaybackService.kt:197, LocalPlaybackHelper.kt:104, SmbPlaybackHelper.kt:120, SftpPlaybackHelper.kt:115, FtpPlaybackHelper.kt:106, CloudPlaybackHelper.kt:71, StreamPlaybackHelper.kt:72, AudioEmptyStateController.kt:257. title: Broad catch (e: Exception) swallows CancellationException from loadPlaylistJob.cancel(), logging normal teardown cancellation as an error

title: releasePlaybackResources() dereferences lateinit playbackController - every pre-initialization teardown path crashes with UninitializedPropertyAccessException

title: shutdownRenderThreadSync abandons a still-alive render thread that strongly references the Activity and the live native EGL/OpenXR session on join timeout
evidence: Lines 1120-1128: `thread.requestExit(); thread.join(timeoutMs); if (thread.isAlive) { Timber.w("...render thread did not exit within ${timeoutMs}ms") }; renderThread = null; sessionReady = false`. DiagnosticXrRenderThread holds `private val activity: Activity` (DiagnosticXrRenderThread.kt line 29) plus three activity method references (onSessionReady/onExitDelivered/onStartFailed, lines 46-48) and blocks inside `runtime.runFrameLoop()` (line 107). If the native frame loop does not observe the exit flag within PAUSE_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS=2000 (onPause) / SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_MS=3000 (onDestroy), the only reference is nulled while the thread keeps running: the destroyed Activity stays reachable from a live thread and the EGL/OpenXR session survives host teardown, with no retry/re-join/watchdog left to reclaim either. The ExoPlayer itself is not affected (released at lines 1106/1112 before the join), so this is a residual-resource path, not a player leak; per taxonomy this is missing lifecycle-awareness without a proven leak -> P2.
fix_hint: After a timed-out join, keep a weak handle and escalate (second join on onDestroy, or a watchdog that logs/reports if the thread is still alive N seconds later); ensure the thread's callbacks null out or no-op once abandoned so a late finally-block cannot call into a destroyed Activity.

title: False load-bearing comment on windowFocusedDeferred: claims a new instance is created in maybeStartRenderThread, but no recreation exists - the focus gate is permanently open for any second render-thread start within one Activity instance

Grep confirms windowFocusedDeferred appears only at field init (line 114, declared `var` suggesting lost reassignment intent), complete() (line 1050) and constructor pass-through (line 1086) - maybeStartRenderThread (lines 1069-1094) never recreates it. Consequence: after the first onWindowFocusChanged(true), a later render-thread start in the same instance (onResume line 1057-1062 / surfaceCreated line 1053) hands the render thread an already-completed Deferred, so the HzOS volumetric-window-registration wait (DiagnosticXrRenderThread.kt lines 80-94, added to fix the re-entry black-screen) is skipped; impact is bounded by the 5 s withTimeoutOrNull fallback and by onRenderThreadExit auto-finishing paused sessions, so the confirmed defect is the comment/`var` contradiction (Rule 8/9: comments in the affected area are load-bearing).

title: Pending MediaController future escapes onStopListening teardown; late completion registers a listener past the symmetric edge and the next connect orphans the unreleased controller
evidence: Registration is asynchronous: `connectToSession()` (called from `onStartListening`, line 29) builds `val future = MediaController.Builder(this, token).buildAsync()` (line 75) and only in the completion callback does `mediaController = future.get(); mediaController?.addListener(tilePlayerListener)` (lines 78-79). The symmetric teardown edge `onStopListening()` calls `releaseController()` (lines 38-41), but releaseController only handles the already-assigned field: `mediaController?.removeListener(tilePlayerListener); mediaController?.release(); mediaController = null` (lines 124-126) - the in-flight `future` is a local, never stored, never passed to `MediaController.releaseFuture()`. Runtime path: user opens the QS shade (onStartListening -> buildAsync pending), closes it before the binder handshake completes (onStopListening -> releaseController is a no-op, mediaController==null), the future then completes: controller C1 is created and `tilePlayerListener` registered while the tile is no longer listening. On the next shade open, `onStartListening` unconditionally calls `connectToSession()` again (no mediaController guard, line 31-32); its completion overwrites `mediaController = future.get()` - C1 is now unreachable and its `release()` is never called, so its session binder connection to AudioPlaybackService and its registered Player.Listener persist until the TileService process dies (onDestroy releases only the last-assigned controller). Each rapid open/close cycle during a pending connect leaks one more connected MediaController - an unreleased heavy resource whose registration escapes the symmetric onStartListening/onStopListening pair via the async path.
fix_hint: Track the future in a field; in releaseController() call MediaController.releaseFuture(pendingFuture) and null it; in the completion callback, bail out (releasing the built controller) if listening has already stopped or a newer future superseded it.

title: connect()/connectForStatus() overwrite controllerFuture without releasing the in-flight future, so one of two interleaved connects leaves a MediaController that release() can never free
evidence: Both entry points do `val future = MediaController.Builder(context, sessionToken).buildAsync(); controllerFuture = future` (lines 63-64 in connect(), 257-258 in connectForStatus()) guarded only by `if (isConnected)` - which stays false while the first future is still pending (`isConnected` reads `mediaController?.isConnected == true`, line 40, and `mediaController` is set only in the completion callback, lines 68-69 / 262-263). The single removal point is `release()`: `controllerFuture?.let { MediaController.releaseFuture(it) }` (line 311) - it releases only the LAST assigned future. Runtime path on one shared instance (PlayerManagerInitializer.kt:715 creates one AudioServiceController per PlayerActivity; NowPlayingManager.kt:155 calls connectForStatus on it, PlayerMediaLoaderManager's playAudioViaService calls connect on it): PlayerActivity opens on a photo while background audio is running - NowPlayingManager.updateBarVisibility fires connectForStatus (future1 pending); the user taps an audio file inside the connect window - connect() sees isConnected==false and overwrites `controllerFuture` with future2. Whichever future completes, future1 is no longer referenced anywhere, so its built MediaController is never passed to releaseFuture - on PlayerLifecycleManager.releaseResources() (line 190 `activity.audioServiceController?.release()`) only future2 is released, leaving future1's controller and its session binder connection to AudioPlaybackService alive for the rest of the process. Asymmetry class: re-registration without removing/releasing the previous registration; window is milliseconds (local binder connect), so no proven leak in normal use - P2 per taxonomy.
fix_hint: Before assigning a new future, release the previous one: `controllerFuture?.let { MediaController.releaseFuture(it) }` at the top of connect() and connectForStatus() (mirroring NowPlayingViewModel.disconnect(), which already releases the pending future before reconnecting).

title: Contract item 2: no onStop handling - video/audio playback keeps running while the host activity is stopped; onCleared is the only teardown edge
evidence: The sole teardown is `override fun onCleared() { .. exoPlayer.removeListener(playerListener); exoPlayer.release() }` (VideoPlayerViewModel.kt:333-343; same in AudioPlayerViewModel.kt:301-309). Grep over wear/src/main for `onStop|onPause|Ambient|LifecycleEventObserver|LocalLifecycleOwner|repeatOnLifecycle` returns no matches; MainActivity has only `onCreate` (MainActivity.kt:41). Runtime path: user plays a video, presses home/palm-over (activity ON_STOP, composition retained, VM alive) - the per-VM ExoPlayer keeps decoding video+audio invisibly on the watch until the OS kills the process; there is no foreground service or MediaSession legitimizing background playback. The S0725 comments (VideoPlayerViewModel.kt:339-341, WearAppModule.kt:58-63) document per-VM ownership vs the old singleton but do not document a deliberate keep-playing-while-stopped decision, so the protocol's 'release in onStop / recreate in onStart, or a deliberate documented alternative' is not met for the ON_STOP edge. No proven leak (release still happens at VM clear) - P2 missing lifecycle-awareness.
fix_hint: Observe host lifecycle (e.g. LifecycleEventObserver or collectAsStateWithLifecycle-driven callback) and at least exoPlayer.pause() on ON_STOP for both VMs; or document background audio as intended and back it with a MediaSession + foreground service.

title: Contract item 5: player never requests audio focus - builder omits setAudioAttributes(attrs, handleAudioFocus=true)
evidence: `return androidx.media3.exoplayer.ExoPlayer.Builder(context).setHandleAudioBecomingNoisy(true).build()` (WearAppModule.kt:68-70). Media3 1.2.1 ExoPlayer.Builder defaults to AudioAttributes.DEFAULT with handleAudioFocus=false, so neither the audio nor the video player ever requests audio focus. Runtime path: start music in AudioPlayerScreen while another watch app (or paired-headphones stream) is playing - both audio streams mix; conversely other apps starting playback do not pause/duck this player. The release-side of item 5 is vacuous (nothing to abandon; release() is called in both VMs), but 'focus handling' per the unit contract is absent entirely.
fix_hint: Build with .setAudioAttributes(AudioAttributes.Builder().setUsage(C.USAGE_MEDIA).setContentType(C.AUDIO_CONTENT_TYPE_MUSIC/MOVIE).build(), /* handleAudioFocus= */ true); release() then abandons focus automatically.

title: Contract item 5 (playWhenReady reset): audio STATE_ENDED seeks to 0 without pausing - track restarts and loops indefinitely
evidence: `Player.STATE_ENDED -> { _uiState.update { it.copy(isPlaying = false, currentPositionMs = 0) }; exoPlayer.seekTo(0); publishPlaybackState() }` (AudioPlayerViewModel.kt:92-96). playWhenReady is set true at load (lines 150, 198) and never reset before the seek; seeking out of STATE_ENDED with playWhenReady=true resumes playback (standard ExoPlayer replay semantics), so every track end restarts the track - an unintended infinite repeat that also burns watch battery and publishes isPlaying=false to the phone while audio is actually playing again. The video VM explicitly avoids this: `exoPlayer.pause(); exoPlayer.seekTo(0)` with comment 'Seek to start for replay, but pause' (VideoPlayerViewModel.kt:93-95).
fix_hint: Mirror the video handler: call exoPlayer.pause() before exoPlayer.seekTo(0) in the STATE_ENDED branch.

title: SMB playback temp files are re-downloaded every open and never deleted - cache dirs grow without app-side bound on watch storage
evidence: `val cacheDir = File(context.cacheDir, "smb_video"); cacheDir.mkdirs(); .. val tempFile = File(cacheDir, tempFileName) .. FileOutputStream(tempFile).use { output -> input.copyTo(output) }` (VideoPlayerViewModel.kt:207-221); identical pattern in AudioPlayerViewModel.kt:174-188 (`smb_audio`). Grep for `cacheDir|smb_video|smb_audio` across wear/src/main shows only these writers - no delete/trim anywhere, and no exists-check, so each playback of an SMB file re-downloads the full media over SMB and overwrites the temp file, while distinct files accumulate forever. Runtime path: browse an SMB source and play N different videos - N full video files pile up in cacheDir on a small-storage watch until OS storage-pressure cache trimming (the only backstop, hence P2 rather than the taxonomy's P1 for unbounded in-memory caches). Cancelled mid-download coroutines also leave partial files behind. Same out-of-unit pattern exists in ImageViewerViewModel.kt:105-110 (`smb_images`) - /spec-draft candidate for the caller.
fix_hint: Reuse an existing complete temp file (skip download), delete the temp file in onCleared, and/or LRU-trim the smb_* cache dirs to a fixed byte budget; apply the same fix to ImageViewerViewModel.

title: First-run video never auto-starts: dismissBatteryWarning does not set playWhenReady although the load path defers autoplay to dismissal

But `fun dismissBatteryWarning() { prefs.edit().putBoolean(KEY_BATTERY_WARNING_SHOWN, true).apply(); _uiState.update { it.copy(showBatteryWarning = false) } }` (lines 156-159) never sets playWhenReady, so on the very first video open the prepared player stays paused after the warning is dismissed and the user must tap play manually - contradicting the stated intent of the comment.

title: PooledConnection.pooledChannels (plain ArrayList) is mutated/iterated under three different lock domains plus lock-free paths - CME/lost-channel race between ExoPlayer loader thread and IO coroutines
evidence: Declaration line 55: `val pooledChannels: MutableList<PooledChannel> = mutableListOf()`. FILE_OPS path adds/removes under sessionMutex: line 173 `pooled.sessionMutex.withLock {` .. line 182 `pooled.pooledChannels.add(pc)`; removeChannel line 192-197 also under sessionMutex. PLAYBACK path adds under a DIFFERENT lock (openChannelLock): line 356 `pooled.openChannelLock.lock()` .. line 370 `pooled.pooledChannels.add(PooledChannel(ch, Mutex(), ChannelPurpose.PLAYBACK))`. evictPlaybackChannel iterates and removes with NO lock at all: lines 458-463 `pooledSessions.values.forEach { pooled -> val target = pooled.pooledChannels.firstOrNull { ... } ... pooled.pooledChannels.remove(target)`; releaseExoPlayerConnection iterates lock-free at 443-444 `pooled.pooledChannels.any { it.channel == channel }`; invalidateSession/cleanupIdleConnections/disconnectAll forEach the list holding only poolMutex (257, 303, 543). sessionMutex, openChannelLock and poolMutex are three independent locks, so none of these accesses mutually exclude each other. Runtime path: SFTP video playing (SftpDataSource.getConnectionForExoPlayer/releaseExoPlayerConnection run on the Media3 loader thread, SftpDataSource.kt:75/236) while thumbnail scans / file ops on the same host run withConnection() on Dispatchers.IO (SftpConnectionPool.kt:90) - concurrent ArrayList add/remove/iterate on the same session's channel list yields ConcurrentModificationException or a lost/duplicated element (channel never disconnected).
fix_hint: Pick one guard for all pooledChannels access (e.g. always sessionMutex, or replace with CopyOnWriteArrayList) and route the blocking PLAYBACK path and evict/release/iterate paths through it.

title: Session-creation TOCTOU: suspend path guards pooledSessions with poolMutex while ExoPlayer blocking path guards it with synchronized(pooledSessions) - duplicate JSch sessions, loser leaks socket + keep-alive thread and its borrow count is never decremented
evidence: Suspend path getOrCreateSession: line 207 `poolMutex.lock()` .. line 209 `val existing = pooledSessions[key]` .. line 235 `pooledSessions[key] = pooled`. Blocking path getOrCreateSessionBlocking: line 410 `synchronized(pooledSessions) {` .. line 411 `val existing = pooledSessions[key]` .. line 434 `pooledSessions[key] = pooled` (comment on 409 claims this avoids TOCTOU, but it uses a different lock than the suspend path, so they do not exclude each other). Runtime path: user starts SFTP video playback (Media3 loader thread -> getConnectionForExoPlayer -> getOrCreateSessionBlocking) while a thumbnail/file-op coroutine on Dispatchers.IO calls withConnection -> getOrCreateSession for the same host - both see existing==null, both connect a JSch session (line 230/432 session.connect), the second map put overwrites the first. The overwritten PooledConnection stays connected (keep-alive thread per lines 228-229/430-431) but is unreachable by cleanup (cleanupIdleConnections iterates only pooledSessions). If the orphan is the PLAYBACK one, releaseExoPlayerConnection (443-446) searches pooledSessions.values for its channel, finds nothing, decrements no counter and never disconnects it - permanent SSH session/socket leak per occurrence.
fix_hint: Use a single lock for both creation paths (e.g. make the blocking path use runBlocking-free poolMutex.tryLock loop or route both through one synchronized(pooledSessions) monitor), or putIfAbsent + disconnect-the-loser.

title: AppWidgetProvider.onUpdate blocks the main thread on Room + gzip + Gson + file-stat via runBlocking (no goAsync/IO dispatch, unlike the fixed ScheduledTasksWidgetProvider)

title: Pending MediaController buildAsync future not released on onStopListening - connection completing after the release edge yields an orphaned, never-released MediaController with a stuck Player.Listener and a leaked ServiceConnection that keeps AudioPlaybackService alive
evidence:
connectToSession() discards the future and the completion callback has no released/still-listening guard:
```kotlin
private fun connectToSession() {
    val token = SessionToken(this, ComponentName(this, AudioPlaybackService::class.java))
    val future = MediaController.Builder(this, token).buildAsync()   // line 75: future is a local, never retained
    future.addListener({
        try {
            mediaController = future.get()                            // line 78: unconditional field assignment
            mediaController?.addListener(tilePlayerListener)          // line 79
```
releaseController() only handles an already-assigned controller - it cannot release an in-flight build because the field is still null and there is no MediaController.releaseFuture() call:
```kotlin
private fun releaseController() {          // line 123
    mediaController?.removeListener(tilePlayerListener)
    mediaController?.release()
    mediaController = null
}
```
Concrete runtime path (all steps on the main looper, so it is a message-ordering hole, not a visibility race): (1) QS shade opens while audio plays -> onStartListening (line 31) -> connectToSession() starts the async bind/handshake to AudioPlaybackService; (2) user closes the shade before the handshake finishes -> onStopListening (line 40) -> releaseController() no-ops (field null, no future to release); (3) the connection-complete message runs the callback -> a live connected MediaController is stored in the field and tilePlayerListener is added, on a tile that is no longer listening; (4) user reopens the shade -> onStartListening -> connectToSession() runs again unconditionally (no existing-controller check, lines 31-33) and its callback overwrites the field at line 78 WITHOUT releasing the previous instance. The first controller is now permanently orphaned: release() is never called on it, tilePlayerListener is never removed (contract items 1, 4, 7), and its internal ServiceConnection stays bound to AudioPlaybackService, preventing the MediaSessionService from stopping itself after playback ends (service + session linger) until the TileService itself is destroyed and the system force-cleans the leaked connection (logcat 'ServiceConnection leaked'). The project already has the correct pattern in the two sibling controller hosts, which this file skips: NowPlayingViewModel.kt lines 62/106/143 (`controllerFuture?.let { MediaController.releaseFuture(it) }`) and AudioServiceController.kt line 311 (`controllerFuture?.let { MediaController.releaseFuture(it) }`).
fix_hint: Retain the future in a field (private var controllerFuture: ListenableFuture<MediaController>? = null; controllerFuture = future in connectToSession). In releaseController() call controllerFuture?.let { MediaController.releaseFuture(it) }; controllerFuture = null before nulling mediaController - releaseFuture releases the controller even if the future completes after the call, mirroring NowPlayingViewModel.disconnect() and AudioServiceController.release().
